title.raw: 卷64 郭祚 張彝 Volume 64: Guo Zuo, Zhang Yi

sentences.zh: 郭祚 張彝

translations.literal: Guo Zuo; Zhang Yi
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zuo; Zhang Yi

sentences.zh: 郭祚，字季祐，太原晉陽人，魏車騎郭淮弟亮後也。

translations.literal: Guo Zuo, courtesy name Jiyou, was a native of Jinyang in Taiyuan, a descendant of Guo Liang, younger brother of Guo Huai, Chariot-and-Cavalry General of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zuo, whose courtesy name was Jiyou, came from Jinyang in Taiyuan and was descended from Guo Liang, the younger brother of the Wei general Guo Huai.

sentences.zh: 祖逸，州別駕，前後以二女妻司徒崔浩，一女妻浩弟上黨太守恬。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yi was a regional aide-de-camp; successively he gave two daughters in marriage to Grand Commandant Cui Hao, and one daughter in marriage to Hao's younger brother Tian, Administrator of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yi had served as regional aide-de-camp and, over time, married two daughters to Grand Commandant Cui Hao and one daughter to Hao's younger brother Tian, the Administrator of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 世祖時，浩親寵用事，拜逸徐州刺史，假榆次侯，終贈光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the reign of Emperor Shizu, Hao enjoyed intimate favor and held power; Yi was appointed Inspector of Xuzhou, enfeoffed provisionally as Marquis of Yuci, and at death was posthumously awarded Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Taiwu, when Hao was in intimate favor and wielded real power, Yi was made Inspector of Xuzhou and provisionally enfeoffed as Marquis of Yuci; after his death he was posthumously honored as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 父洪之，坐浩事誅，祚亡竄得免。

translations.literal: His father Hongzhi, implicated in Hao's affair, was executed; Zuo fled in hiding and escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hongzhi was executed in connection with Cui Hao's downfall, but Zuo went into hiding and survived.

sentences.zh: 少而孤貧，姿貌不偉，鄉人莫之識也。

translations.literal: From youth he was orphaned and poor; his appearance was not imposing, and the people of his district did not know him.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor from boyhood, without a striking appearance, he was hardly known among his neighbors.

sentences.zh: 有女巫相祚後當富貴。

translations.literal: A shamaness divined that Zuo would later attain wealth and rank.
translations.idiomatic: A village shamaness foretold that Zuo would one day rise to wealth and high office.

sentences.zh: 祚涉歷經史，習崔浩之書，尺牘文章見稱於世。

translations.literal: Zuo ranged through the classics and histories and studied the writings of Cui Hao; his letters and essays won renown in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He steeped himself in the classics and histories, studied Cui Hao's works, and gained a reputation for his letters and literary compositions.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，州主簿，刺史孫小委之書記。

translations.literal: At the age of twenty he became a provincial chief clerk; the inspector Sun Xiao entrusted him with secretarial duties.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he became chief clerk of his province, and the inspector Sun Xiao put him in charge of secretarial work.

sentences.zh: 又太原王希者，逸妻之姪，共相賙恤，得以饒振。

translations.literal: Moreover, Wang Xi of Taiyuan, a nephew on his wife's side of Yi, mutually supported and relieved one another, and thereby he was able to recover prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xi of Taiyuan, a nephew by marriage of his grandfather Yi, also helped support him, and together they managed to restore his fortunes.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，舉秀才，對策上第，拜中書博士，轉中書侍郎，遷尚書左丞，長兼給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozu's reign, he was recommended as a xiucai, ranked first class in the policy examination, appointed Doctor of the Secretariat, transferred to Secretariat Gentleman, promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and for a long time concurrently served as Supervising Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the reign of Emperor Wen, he was nominated as an outstanding scholar, placed first in the court examination, and rose through appointments as Doctor of the Secretariat and Secretariat Gentleman to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, while also serving for a long time as Supervising Attendant of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 祚清勤在公，夙夜匪懈，高祖甚知賞之。

translations.literal: Zuo was pure and diligent in office, never slackening day or night; Emperor Gaozu deeply appreciated him.
translations.idiomatic: Clear-handed and tireless in public office, he won Emperor Wen's keen esteem.

sentences.zh: 從高祖南征，及還，正黃門。

translations.literal: He accompanied Emperor Gaozu on the southern campaign, and upon return was made Regular Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the emperor on the southern campaign, and on their return was made a full Attendant of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸長安，行經渭橋，過郭淮廟，問祚曰：「是卿祖宗所承也？」

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage visited Chang'an and passed the Wei Bridge, it went by the shrine of Guo Huai, and [the emperor] asked Zuo, "Is this the forebear your family receives in succession?"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Chang'an and passed the Wei Bridge, he came by Guo Huai's shrine and asked Zuo, "Is this the ancestor your line inherits?"

sentences.zh: 祚曰：「是臣七世伯祖。」

translations.literal: Zuo said, "He is this subject's seventh-generation grand uncle."
translations.idiomatic: Zuo replied, "He is my seventh-generation grand uncle."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「先賢後哲，頓在一門。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said, "Worthy predecessors and brilliant successors, all concentrated in one clan."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Ancient worthies and present sages, all gathered in a single house."

sentences.zh: 祚對曰：「昔臣先人以通儒英博，唯事魏文，微臣虛薄，遭奉明聖，自惟幸甚。」

translations.literal: Zuo replied, "In former days my forebears, as broadly learned erudites, served only Emperor Wen of Wei; this petty subject, empty and slight, has encountered and received an enlightened sage—by my own reckoning, I am most fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: Zuo answered, "My ancestors were encyclopedic scholars who served only Cao Wen, Emperor of Wei; as for me, a man of little merit, to meet so sage an emperor is fortune beyond what I deserve."

sentences.zh: 因敕以太牢祭淮廟，令祚自撰祭文。

translations.literal: Thereupon he commanded that the grand sacrificial victim be used to sacrifice at Huai's shrine, and ordered Zuo himself to compose the sacrificial text.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered a grand sacrifice at Huai's shrine and had Zuo compose the funeral ode himself.

sentences.zh: 以贊遷洛之規，賜爵東光子。

translations.literal: For supporting the plan of moving the capital to Luoyang, he was granted the title Viscount of Dongguang.
translations.idiomatic: For his support of the move to Luoyang, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Dongguang.

sentences.zh: 高祖曾幸華林園，因觀故景陽山，祚曰：「山以仁靜，水以智流，願陛下修之。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu once visited the Hualin Park and observed the old Jingyang Hill; Zuo said, "Mountains embody benevolent stillness and waters embody intelligent flow—may Your Majesty cultivate these."
translations.idiomatic: On a visit to Hualin Park, where the emperor took in the old site of Jingyang Hill, Zuo said, "Mountains express benevolence in their stillness and water wisdom in its flow—may Your Majesty restore them."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「魏明以奢失於前，朕何為襲之於後？」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said, "Emperor Ming of Wei ruined himself through extravagance in the past—why should I repeat this afterward?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Emperor Ming of Wei lost everything to extravagance—why should I follow his example?"

sentences.zh: 祚曰：「高山仰止。」

translations.literal: Zuo said, "One looks up to a high mountain."
translations.idiomatic: Zuo said only, "One looks up to a high mountain."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「得非景行之謂？」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said, "May this not refer to a 'road worth admiring'?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Do you mean the path one ought to admire?"

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍，仍領黃門。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary, and still headed the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary while retaining direction of the Yellow Gate office.

sentences.zh: 是時高祖銳意典禮，兼銓鏡九流，又遷都草創，征討不息，內外規略，號為多事。

translations.literal: At this time Emperor Gaozu was keen on rituals and regulations, and also examined and mirrored the Nine Categories; moreover the move of the capital was newly undertaken and campaigns of conquest did not cease—the inner and outer administrative schemes were called extremely busy.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor was pressing ahead with ritual reform and screening talent across every walk of office, even as the new capital was still being built and campaigns continued without pause; court and realm alike were said to be overwhelmed with affairs.

sentences.zh: 祚與黃門宋弁參謀幃幄，隨其才用，各有委寄。

translations.literal: Zuo and Song Bian of the Yellow Gate planned within the curtain of the throne, and according to their talents each received respective commissions.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo and Song Bian of the Yellow Gate advised him within the privy council, each entrusted with tasks suited to his talent.

sentences.zh: 祚承禀注疏，特成勤劇。

translations.literal: Zuo undertook receipt of imperial notes and commentary, and became especially laborious and strenuous.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo took charge of drafting imperial instructions and commentaries, work that proved especially demanding.

sentences.zh: 嘗以立馮昭儀，百官夕飲清徽後園，高祖舉觴賜祚及崔光曰：「郭祚憂勞庶事，獨不欺我；

translations.literal: Once, on establishing Lady Feng as Honored Imperial Concubine, the officials drank in the evening in the garden behind Qinghui; Emperor Gaozu raised his cup and bestowed it upon Zuo and Cui Guang, saying, "Guo Zuo worries over the multitude of affairs and alone does not deceive me;
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion, when Lady Feng was installed as Honored Imperial Concubine, the officials feasted in the evening in the garden behind Qinghui; the emperor raised his goblet toward Zuo and Cui Guang and said, "Guo Zuo shoulders the realm's business and never deceives me;

sentences.zh: 崔光溫良博物，朝之儒秀。

translations.literal: Cui Guang is gentle and good, learned in many things—the scholarly elite of the court.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang is mild, learned, and the court's finest scholar.

sentences.zh: 不勸此兩人，當勸誰也？」

translations.literal: If one does not toast these two men, whom should one toast?"
translations.idiomatic: If I do not raise a toast to these two, whom should I toast?"

sentences.zh: 其見知若此。

translations.literal: Such was the degree of his recognition.
translations.idiomatic: This was how highly he was regarded.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖以李彪為散騎常侍，祚因入見，高祖謂祚曰：「朕昨誤授一人官。」

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Gaozu had appointed Li Biao as Attendant-in-Ordinary; when Zuo came in for an audience, Emperor Gaozu said to him, "Yesterday I mistakenly granted an office to someone."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had appointed Li Biao Attendant-in-Ordinary; when Zuo came in for an audience, the emperor told him, "Yesterday I gave an office to the wrong man."

sentences.zh: 祚對曰：「陛下聖鏡照臨，論才授職，進退可否，黜陟幽明，品物既彰，人倫有序，豈容聖詔一行而有差異。」

translations.literal: Zuo replied, "Your Majesty's sacred mirror shines upon all; talents are weighed in granting offices, advancement and demotion are decided on merit, the obscure and the manifest are promoted or demoted, all things are made clear and human order is settled—how could a single imperial edict be issued with error?"
translations.idiomatic: Zuo replied, "Your Majesty's judgment is infallible; you weigh talent in every appointment, promote and demote on merit, and keep the whole order of the realm in balance—how could a single edict be mistaken?"

sentences.zh: 高祖沉吟曰：「此自應有讓，因讓，朕欲別授一官。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu mused and said, "This man ought by rights to decline; because he declines, I wish to grant another office."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor paused and said, "He ought to decline the post; once he does, I mean to give him something else."

sentences.zh: 須臾，彪有啟云：「伯石辭卿，子產所惡，臣欲之已久，不敢辭讓。」

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Biao submitted a memorial saying, "When Boshi declined a ministerial post, Zichan detested it; your subject has long desired this office and dares not decline."
translations.idiomatic: A moment later Biao submitted a memorial: "When Boshi declined a ministry, Zichan despised the pretense; I have wanted this post for a long time and dare not decline it."

sentences.zh: 高祖歎謂祚曰：「卿之忠諫，李彪正辭，使朕遲回不能復決。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu sighed and said to Zuo, "Your loyal remonstrance and Li Biao's upright words make me hesitate and unable to decide again."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed and told Zuo, "Your loyal counsel and Li Biao's forthright reply leave me unable to settle the matter."

sentences.zh: 遂不換彪官也。

translations.literal: Thereupon he did not change Biao's office.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he left Biao in his post.

sentences.zh: 乘輿南討，祚以兼侍中從，拜尚書，進爵為伯。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage went south on campaign, Zuo followed as Acting Palace Attendant, was appointed Director of the Department of State Affairs, and advanced in rank to Baron.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern campaign Zuo accompanied the emperor as Acting Palace Attendant, was made Director of the Department of State Affairs, and raised to the rank of baron.

sentences.zh: 高祖崩，咸陽王禧等奏祚兼吏部尚書，尋除長兼吏部尚書、并州大中正。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu died, the Prince of Xianyang, Xi, and others memorialized that Zuo should concurrently serve as Director of the Ministry of Personnel; soon afterward he was appointed long-term concurrent Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Grand Rectifier of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wen's death, the Prince of Xianyang and others recommended that Zuo serve concurrently as Director of the Ministry of Personnel; he was soon made permanent concurrent director of that ministry and Grand Rectifier of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 世宗詔以姦吏逃刑，懸配遠戍，若永避不出，兄弟代之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong issued an edict that corrupt officials who fled punishment should be registered for assignment to distant garrison service; if they permanently avoided appearing, their brothers were to serve in their place.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu decreed that corrupt officials who evaded punishment should be registered for exile to distant garrisons, and if they never surrendered, their brothers would serve the sentence in their stead.

sentences.zh: 祚奏曰：「慎獄審刑，道煥先古；

translations.literal: Zuo memorialized, saying, "Care in prisons and deliberation in punishments make the Way shine in antiquity;
translations.idiomatic: Zuo submitted a memorial: "Careful prisons and measured punishments made the Way radiant in antiquity;

sentences.zh: 垂憲設禁，義纂惟今。

translations.literal: to hand down statutes and establish prohibitions gathers meaning only in the present age.
translations.idiomatic: to hand down statutes and establish prohibitions gathers its meaning in our own age alone.

sentences.zh: 是以先王沿物之情，為之軌法，故八刑備於昔典，姦律炳於來制，皆所以謀其始迹，訪厥成罪，敦風厲俗，永資世範者也。

translations.literal: Therefore the former kings followed the feelings of things and made standards and laws for them; thus the Eight Punishments were complete in the ancient canon and statutes against corruption were manifest in later regulations—all to trace the first signs, investigate the completed guilt, strengthen custom and sharpen mores, and provide an everlasting model for the age.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the former kings shaped law to human nature: the Eight Punishments stood complete in the ancient canon, and statutes against corruption shone forth in later codes—all to trace crimes from their first signs, establish guilt when complete, strengthen custom, and supply a lasting model for the world.

sentences.zh: 伏惟旨義博遠，理絕近情，既懷愚異，不容不述。

translations.literal: I bow to consider that the intent of the edict is broad and far-reaching, its principle utterly removed from ordinary feeling; since I harbor foolish doubts, I cannot but set them forth.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's intent is broad and far-reaching, its logic far from ordinary feeling; yet since I harbor doubts, I cannot remain silent.

sentences.zh: 誠以敗法之原，起於姦吏，姦吏雖微，敗法實甚。

translations.literal: Truly the source of destroying the law arises from corrupt officials; though corrupt officials are petty, the destruction of law is in fact grave.
translations.idiomatic: The root of law's ruin lies in corrupt petty officials; small though they are, the harm they do to the law is grave.

sentences.zh: 伏尋詔旨，信亦斷其逋逃之路，為治之要，實在於斯。

translations.literal: I bow to examine the edict's intent: it truly also cuts off their path of flight and evasion; the essential of good government lies indeed in this.
translations.idiomatic: Your decree plainly cuts off their path of escape, and the heart of good government lies precisely there.

sentences.zh: 然法貴止姦，不在過酷，立制施禁，為可傳之於後。

translations.literal: Yet the law values stopping corruption, not excessive severity; to establish regulations and impose prohibitions is so that they may be handed down to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet law should stop corruption, not grow cruel beyond need; regulations are made to endure for generations.

sentences.zh: 若法猛而姦不息，禁過不可永傳，將何以載之刑書，垂之百代？

translations.literal: If the law is fierce yet corruption does not cease, and prohibitions go too far and cannot be handed down forever, how will they be recorded in the books of punishment and handed down through a hundred generations?
translations.idiomatic: If harsh law fails to end corruption, and excessive prohibitions cannot endure, how are they to be written into the penal codes and handed down through the ages?

sentences.zh: 若以姦吏逃竄，徙其兄弟，罪人妻子復應從之，此則一人之罪，禍傾二室。

translations.literal: If because a corrupt official flees and absconds his brothers are relocated, and the criminal's wife and children must likewise follow, then for one man's guilt calamity overturns two households.
translations.idiomatic: If a fleeing corrupt official's brothers are exiled, and his wife and children must follow as well, one man's crime would ruin two whole families.

sentences.zh: 愚謂罪人既逃，止徙妻子，走者之身，懸名永配，於眚不免，姦途自塞。」

translations.literal: This foolish subject holds that once the criminal has fled, only his wife and children should be relocated; the fugitive's person should be registered by name for perpetual assignment, not exempted even in amnesties, and the path of corruption will of itself be blocked.
translations.idiomatic: I suggest that once the culprit has fled, only his wife and children be relocated, while the fugitive himself remain registered for perpetual exile, never pardoned even in general amnesties—so the road to corruption closes by itself.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: The edict followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 尋正吏部。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was made regular Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made full Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 祚持身潔清，重惜官位，至於銓授，假令得人，必徘徊久之，然後下筆，下筆即云：「此人便以貴矣。」

translations.literal: Zuo maintained himself in purity and integrity and greatly cherished official rank; as for selection and appointment, even when he had found the right man, he would always hesitate for a long time before putting brush to paper, and once he wrote he would say, "This man has now been made noble."
translations.idiomatic: Scrupulous in his personal conduct and deeply reluctant to confer rank, he would linger long over every appointment even when he had found the right man; only after prolonged hesitation would he set brush to paper, remarking as he did so, "This man has now been ennobled."

sentences.zh: 由是事頗稽滯，當時每招怨讟。

translations.literal: Because of this affairs were rather delayed, and at the time he often drew resentment and slander.
translations.idiomatic: Business therefore dragged, and he often drew resentment at the time.

sentences.zh: 然所拔用者，皆量才稱職，時又以此歸之。

translations.literal: Yet those he promoted and employed were all measured by talent and matched to office, and the age in turn credited him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those he promoted were always well matched to their posts, and contemporaries credited him for that.

sentences.zh: 出為使持節、鎮北將軍、瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Who Pacifies the North, and Inspector of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Who Pacifies the North, and Inspector of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 及太極殿成，祚朝於京師，轉鎮東將軍、青州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Hall of Supreme Ultimate was completed, Zuo came to court in the capital and was transferred to General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hall of Supreme Ultimate was completed, he attended court in the capital and was transferred to General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 祚值歲不稔，闔境飢弊，矜傷愛下，多所賑恤，雖斷決淹留，號為煩緩，然士女懷其德澤，于今思之。

translations.literal: Zuo encountered years of poor harvest; throughout his jurisdiction there was hunger and distress; he pitied and cared for those below and gave much relief and succor; though his judgments were delayed and he was called troublesome and slow, yet men and women cherished his benevolent favor and still remember him today.
translations.idiomatic: During years of poor harvest, when hunger spread through his whole jurisdiction, he showed compassion to the people and gave generous relief; though his legal decisions were slow and he was criticized as dilatory, the people cherished his kindness and remember him still.

sentences.zh: 入為侍中、金紫光祿大夫、并州大中正，遷尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He entered court as Palace Attendant, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and Grand Rectifier of Bing Province, and was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as Palace Attendant, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and Grand Rectifier of Bing Province, and was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時議定新令，詔祚與侍中、黃門參議刊正。

translations.literal: At that time the new statutes were being discussed and decided; an edict ordered Zuo, together with the Palace Attendant and the Yellow Gate, to participate in deliberation and revision.
translations.idiomatic: When new statutes were being drafted, the emperor ordered Zuo, together with the Palace Attendant and the Yellow Gate office, to join in revising them.

sentences.zh: 故事，令、僕、中丞騶唱而入宮門，至於馬道。

translations.literal: By precedent, directors, vice directors, and chief censors entered the palace gate with mounted attendants calling the way, all the way to the horse ramp.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, directors, vice directors, and chief censors entered the palace gate with mounted attendants announcing their approach, all the way to the horse ramp.

sentences.zh: [1]及祚為僕射，以為非盡敬之宜，言於世宗，帝納之，下詔：「御在太極，騶唱至止車門；

translations.literal: When Zuo became Vice Director, he held that this was not fully appropriate to utmost respect and spoke to Emperor Shizong; the emperor accepted it and issued an edict: "When the emperor is in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, mounted attendants shall call the way only to the Gate Where Chariots Stop;
translations.idiomatic: When Zuo became Vice Director, he argued that this fell short of full respect and spoke to Emperor Xuanwu; the emperor agreed and decreed: "When the emperor is in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, mounted attendants shall announce the approach only as far as the Gate Where Chariots Stop;

sentences.zh: 御在朝堂，至司馬門。」

translations.literal: when the emperor is in the Audience Hall, only to the Sima Gate."
translations.idiomatic: when the emperor is in the Audience Hall, only as far as the Sima Gate."

sentences.zh: 騶唱不入宮，自此始也。

translations.literal: Mounted attendants calling the way did not enter the palace—from this it began.
translations.idiomatic: From that time mounted attendants ceased announcing officials inside the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 詔祚本官領太子少師。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zuo to retain his original office while also heading the Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Zuo to retain his present office while also serving as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 祚曾從世宗幸東宮，肅宗幼弱，祚懷一黃㼐出奉肅宗。

translations.literal: Zuo once accompanied Emperor Shizong on a visit to the Eastern Palace; Emperor Suzong was young and weak, and Zuo took out a yellow purse from his bosom and presented it to Suzong.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when Zuo accompanied Emperor Xuanwu to the Eastern Palace, the young heir Emperor Suzong was still a child; Zuo drew a yellow purse from his robe and offered it to him.

sentences.zh: 時應詔左右趙桃弓與御史中尉王顯迭相脣齒，深為世宗所信，祚私事之。

translations.literal: At that time Zhao Taogong of the Attendants in Attendance on Imperial Edicts and Wang Xian, Chief Censor, were mutually dependent like lips and teeth and were deeply trusted by Emperor Shizong; Zuo privately cultivated them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhao Taogong of the Attendants in Attendance on Imperial Edicts and Wang Xian, Chief Censor, were closely allied and deeply trusted by the emperor; Zuo cultivated them in private.

sentences.zh: 時人謗祚者，號為桃弓僕射、黃㼐少師。

translations.literal: Those who slandered Zuo at the time called him "Peach-Bow Vice Director" and "Yellow-Purse Junior Tutor."
translations.idiomatic: Those who mocked him called him "Peach-Bow Vice Director" and "Yellow-Purse Junior Tutor."

sentences.zh: 祚奏曰：「謹案前後考格雖班天下，如臣愚短，猶有未悟。

translations.literal: Zuo memorialized, saying, "I respectfully examine that although the former and later examination regulations have been promulgated throughout the realm, such a foolish and short person as I still has points I do not understand.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo submitted a memorial: "Although the examination regulations, old and new, have been promulgated throughout the realm, I am still unclear on several points.

sentences.zh: 今須定職人遷轉由狀，超越階級者即須量折。

translations.literal: Now it is necessary to fix the transfer of officeholders according to dossiers; those who leap over ranks must have deductions measured.
translations.idiomatic: Officeholders' promotions must now be fixed by dossier, and any leap over normal rank must be offset by a measured deduction.

sentences.zh: 景明初考格，五年者得一階半。

translations.literal: Under the Jingming-era initial examination regulations, after five years one gained one and a half ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Under the initial Jingming examination rules, five years of service earned one and a half ranks.

sentences.zh: 正始中，故尚書、中山王英奏考格，被旨：但可正滿三周為限，不得計殘年之勤。

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi era, the late Director of the Department of State Affairs, the Prince of Zhongshan, Ying, memorialized on the examination regulations and received the imperial response: only a full three cycles may serve as the limit; partial years of service may not be counted.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengshi era the late Director Ying, Prince of Zhongshan, submitted regulations on examinations and received the reply that only three full cycles counted and partial years of service could not be tallied.

sentences.zh: 又去年中，以前二制不同，奏請裁決。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the middle of last year, because the two earlier systems differed, a memorial was submitted requesting a ruling.
translations.idiomatic: Last year, because the two earlier systems differed, a memorial was submitted requesting a decision.

sentences.zh: 旨云：『黜陟之體，自依舊來恒斷。』

translations.literal: The imperial response said: "The substance of promotion and demotion shall follow the constant rulings of old."
translations.idiomatic: The imperial reply said: "Promotion and demotion shall follow the standing practice of old."

sentences.zh: 今未審從舊來之旨，為從景明之斷，為從正始為限？

translations.literal: Now it is not yet clear whether to follow the intent of old, to follow the Jingming ruling, or to take Zhengshi as the limit?
translations.idiomatic: It remains unclear whether we should follow the old practice, the Jingming ruling, or the Zhengshi limit.

sentences.zh: 景明考法，東西省文武閑官悉為三等，考同任事，而前尚書盧昶奏上第之人三年轉半階。

translations.literal: Under the Jingming examination method, civil and military idle officials of the Eastern and Western Bureaus were all placed in three grades and examined the same as active officeholders; yet the former Director Lu Chang memorialized that those in the top grade should advance half a rank after three years.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jingming method, idle civil and military officials of the Eastern and Western Bureaus were all placed in three grades and examined like active officeholders; yet the former Director Lu Chang ruled that top-grade men should advance half a rank after three years.

sentences.zh: 今之考格，復分為九等，前後不同，參差無準。」

translations.literal: The present examination regulations again divide into nine grades; former and latter differ, with no consistent standard."
translations.idiomatic: The present regulations again divide candidates into nine grades; the systems differ and leave no consistent standard."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「考在上中者，得汎以前，有六年以上遷一階，三年以上遷半階，殘年悉除。

translations.literal: An edict said: "For those whose examination grade is upper-middle, counting back before the general review, if there are six years or more they advance one rank, if three years or more they advance half a rank, and partial years are all eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: The edict replied: "For those rated upper-middle, counting back before the general review: six years or more earn one full rank, three years or more earn half a rank, and partial years are struck out entirely.

sentences.zh: 考在上下者，得汎以前，六年以上遷半階，不滿者除。

translations.literal: For those whose grade is upper-lower, counting back before the general review, six years or more advance half a rank; those not reaching this are eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: For those rated upper-lower, counting back before the general review: six years or more earn half a rank; anything less is struck out.

sentences.zh: 其得汎以後考在上下者，三年遷一階。

translations.literal: For those who after the general review receive upper-lower, after three years they advance one rank.
translations.idiomatic: After the general review, those rated upper-lower advance one rank every three years.

sentences.zh: 散官從盧昶所奏。」

translations.literal: Idle officials follow what Lu Chang memorialized."
translations.idiomatic: Idle officials follow Lu Chang's memorial."

sentences.zh: 祚又奏言：「考察令：公清獨著，德績超倫，而無負殿者為上上，一殿為上中，二殿為上以為第，隨前後年斷，各自除其善惡而為昇降？

translations.literal: Zuo again memorialized, saying, "The examination ordinance states: outstanding in public integrity alone, virtue and achievement surpassing the norm, and with no demerit marks is upper-upper; one demerit mark is upper-middle, two demerit marks is upper-lower as grades—are promotions and demotions to follow the former or latter year rulings, each eliminating good and bad accordingly?
translations.idiomatic: Zuo submitted another memorial: "The examination ordinance ranks those outstanding in integrity with no demerit marks as upper-upper, one mark as upper-middle, and two marks as upper-lower—are promotions and demotions to follow the former or latter year rules, each striking out merits and faults accordingly?

sentences.zh: 且負注之章，數成殿為差，此條以寡愆為最，多戾為殿。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the chapter on demerit marks, a fixed number of marks constitutes a demerit grade; this article takes few faults as best and many offenses as demerit.
translations.idiomatic: The chapter on demerit marks fixes how many marks constitute a demerit grade, treating few faults as best and many offenses as worst.

sentences.zh: 未審取何行是寡愆？

translations.literal: It is not yet clear which conduct counts as few faults?
translations.idiomatic: Which conduct counts as few faults?

sentences.zh: 何坐為多戾？

translations.literal: Which offenses count as many violations?
translations.idiomatic: Which offenses count as many violations?

sentences.zh: 結累品次，復有幾等？

translations.literal: When demerit marks are totaled into grades, how many levels are there again?
translations.idiomatic: When demerit marks are totaled into grades, how many levels are there?

sentences.zh: 諸文案失衷，應杖十者為一負。

translations.literal: For all documents and cases that miss the mean, those warranting ten blows with the staff count as one demerit.
translations.idiomatic: For all documents and cases that miss the mark, offenses warranting ten blows with the staff count as one demerit mark.

sentences.zh: 罪依律次，過隨負記。

translations.literal: Guilt follows the sequence of the statutes; offenses are recorded according to demerit marks.
translations.idiomatic: Guilt follows the sequence of the statutes, and offenses are recorded by demerit marks.

sentences.zh: 十年之中，三經肆眚，赦前之罪，不問輕重，皆蒙宥免。

translations.literal: Within ten years, if one passes through three general amnesties, crimes before the amnesty, regardless of severity, all receive pardon and exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten years, if one passes through three general amnesties, pre-amnesty crimes, regardless of severity, are all pardoned.

sentences.zh: 或為御史所彈，案驗未周，遇赦復任者，未審記殿得除以不？」

translations.literal: Or if impeached by the censor, the case not yet fully verified, and upon amnesty restored to office—are demerit marks to be eliminated or not?"
translations.idiomatic: Or if impeached by the censor before the case is closed, and upon amnesty restored to office—are demerit marks to be struck out or not?"

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「獨著、超倫及才備、寡咎，皆謂文武兼上上之極言耳。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Outstanding alone, surpassing the norm, and talent complete with few faults—all refer to the utmost expression of upper-upper for civil and military together.
translations.idiomatic: The edict replied: "Outstanding alone, surpassing the norm, and talent complete with few faults—all describe the highest civil and military grade of upper-upper.

sentences.zh: 自此以降，猶有八等，隨才為次，令文已具。

translations.literal: From this downward there are still eight grades, arranged according to talent in sequence; the text of the ordinance is already complete.
translations.idiomatic: Below that there are still eight grades, arranged by talent; the ordinance text already covers them.

sentences.zh: 其積負累殿及守平得濟，皆含在其中，何容別疑也。

translations.literal: The accumulation of demerit marks, cumulative demerit grades, and maintaining the mean to pass—all are included within it; how could there be separate doubts?
translations.idiomatic: Accumulated demerit marks, cumulative demerit grades, and maintaining the mean to pass are all covered there—what room is there for further doubt?

sentences.zh: 所云通考者，據總多年之言，至於黜陟之體，自依舊來年斷，何足復請。

translations.literal: What is called the general review is based on a summation of many years; as for the substance of promotion and demotion, it follows the annual rulings of old—why need you ask again?
translations.idiomatic: The general review sums many years together; promotion and demotion follow the standing annual rules—there is nothing more to ask.

sentences.zh: 其罰贖已決之殿，固非免限，遇赦免罪，惟記其殿，除之。」

translations.literal: Demerit marks for fines and ransoms already decided are certainly not within the scope of exemption; when amnesty pardons guilt, only the demerit marks are recorded and eliminated."
translations.idiomatic: Demerit marks for fines and ransoms already decided are not exempt; when amnesty pardons the crime, only the demerit marks are recorded and then struck out."

sentences.zh: 尋加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was additionally appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon additionally appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 時詔營明堂國學，祚奏曰：「今雲羅西舉，開納岷蜀；

translations.literal: At that time an edict ordered the construction of the Bright Hall and the Imperial Academy; Zuo memorialized, saying, "Now clouds of banners rise in the west, opening and receiving Min and Shu;
translations.idiomatic: When an edict ordered construction of the Bright Hall and the Imperial Academy, Zuo memorialized: "Banners now gather in the west as Min and Shu are brought in;

sentences.zh: 戎旗東指，鎮靖淮荊；

translations.literal: military banners point east, pacifying the Huai and Jing;
translations.idiomatic: military banners point east to pacify the Huai and Jing;

sentences.zh: 漢沔之間復須防捍。

translations.literal: between the Han and Mian rivers defense must again be maintained.
translations.idiomatic: the Han and Mian region again requires defense.

sentences.zh: 徵兵發眾，所在殷廣，邊郊多壘，烽驛未息，不可於師旅之際，興板築之功。

translations.literal: Recruiting soldiers and dispatching masses, everywhere is full and broad; border suburbs have many ramparts; beacon fires and post relays have not ceased—it is not possible amid armies on campaign to undertake construction with boards and earthworks.
translations.idiomatic: Recruitment and mobilization fill every district; border fortresses multiply and beacon fires never rest—it is no time, amid active campaigns, to launch major building works.

sentences.zh: 且獻歲云暨，東作將始，臣愚量謂宜待豐靖之年，因子來之力，可不時而就。」

translations.literal: Moreover, the New Year's sacrifice is at hand and spring plowing is about to begin; in my humble judgment it would be fitting to wait for a year of abundance and tranquility, and by relying on the labor that comes in its season, the work could be completed without undue haste."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the year's offering is nearly due and the eastern fields are about to be broken for planting. In my humble view we ought to wait for a year of plenty and peace, and lean on the strength that the season itself provides—the work could then be finished without forcing the moment.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [The court] followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 世宗末年，每引祚入東宮，密受賞賚，多至百餘萬，雜以錦繡。

translations.literal: In the late years of Emperor Shizong, [the emperor] would frequently summon Zuo to the Eastern Palace, where he secretly received rewards and gifts, often exceeding a million [in value], mixed with brocades and embroideries.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of Emperor Xuanwu's reign, the emperor often had Zuo brought into the Eastern Palace, where in secret he received gifts and grants—sometimes more than a million in value, along with silks and brocades.

sentences.zh: 又特賜以劍杖，恩寵甚深，遷左僕射。

translations.literal: He was also specially granted sword and staff [of authority]; his favor was very deep, and he was promoted to Left Vice Director [of the Secretariat].
translations.idiomatic: He was further granted the sword and staff of high office, and the depth of imperial favor saw him promoted to Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 先是，蕭衍遣將康絢遏淮，將灌揚徐，祚表曰：「蕭衍狂悖，擅斷川瀆，役苦民勞，危亡已兆。

translations.literal: Previously, Xiao Yan sent the general Kang Xuan to block the Huai [River], intending to flood Yang [zhou] and Xu [zhou]. Zuo submitted a memorial saying: "Xiao Yan is wildly defiant; he has arbitrarily cut off rivers and waterways; the conscript labor has bitterly exhausted the people—portents of peril and ruin have already appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xiao Yan had sent the general Kang Xuan to dam the Huai, intending to inundate Yang and Xu. Zuo memorialized the throne: "Xiao Yan is reckless and lawless. He has seized control of rivers and channels at will, grinding the people down with forced labor—the signs of ruin are already plain.

sentences.zh: 然古諺有之，『敵不可縱』。

translations.literal: Yet as an ancient proverb has it, 'One must not leave an enemy unchecked.'
translations.idiomatic: Yet the old saying holds: 'Do not let the enemy go unchecked.'

sentences.zh: 夫以一酌之水，或為不測之淵，如不時滅，恐同原草。

translations.literal: For with a cupful of water, it may become an unfathomable abyss; if it is not extinguished in time, I fear it will spread like grass on the plain.
translations.idiomatic: A single cup of water can become an unfathomable abyss; if it is not crushed in time, I fear it will spread like grass on an open field.

sentences.zh: 宜命一重將，率統軍三十人，領羽林一萬五千人，并科京東七州虎旅九萬，長驅電邁，遄令撲討。

translations.literal: It is fitting to appoint a senior general to lead thirty army commanders, command fifteen thousand Feathered Forest [guards], and also mobilize from the seven eastern capital provinces ninety thousand fierce troops, to drive forward like lightning and swiftly dispatch them to strike down and suppress [the enemy].
translations.idiomatic: We should appoint a senior general to lead thirty commanders of armies, fifteen thousand Feathered Forest guards, and the ninety thousand crack troops of the seven eastern provinces around the capital—then drive forward like lightning and strike at once.

sentences.zh: 擒斬之勳，一如常制，賊資雜物，悉入軍人。

translations.literal: Rewards for capturing and beheading [enemies] should follow the usual regulations; all booty and miscellaneous goods from the rebels should go entirely to the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards for captures and kills should follow the usual rules, and all rebel goods and spoils should go entirely to the troops.

sentences.zh: 如此，則鯨鯢之首可不日而懸。

translations.literal: In this way, the heads of the great whales and crocodiles [the enemy leaders] could be hung up within days.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the heads of the great beasts could be hung up within days.

sentences.zh: 誠知農桑之時，非發眾之日，苟事理宜然，亦不得不爾。

translations.literal: I truly know that this is the season for farming and sericulture, not a time for mobilizing troops; yet if the circumstances and reason demand it, there is no choice but to do so.
translations.idiomatic: I know full well that this is the season of plowing and mulberry, not the season for raising armies; yet when reason and circumstance require it, there is no choice.

sentences.zh: 昔韋顧跋扈，殷后起昆吾之師；

translations.literal: In the past, [the lords of] Wei and Gu were overbearing; Empress Qi of the Shang raised the army of Kunwu;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when Wei and Gu grew overbearing, Empress Qi of the Shang raised the army of Kunwu;

sentences.zh: 玁狁孔熾，周王興六月之伐。

translations.literal: when the Xianyun were intensely rampant, the King of Zhou launched the campaign of the sixth month.
translations.idiomatic: when the Xianyun burned hot, the Zhou king launched the campaign of the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 臣職忝樞衡，獻納是主，心之所懷，寧敢自默。

translations.literal: My office humbly occupies the pivot of state affairs; my chief duty is to offer and accept [counsel]; what rests in my heart—how dare I keep silent?
translations.idiomatic: My post touches the pivot of the realm, and my charge is to speak and to counsel. What I carry in my heart—how could I keep silent?

sentences.zh: 并宜敕揚州選一猛將，遣當州之兵令赴浮山，表裏夾攻。」

translations.literal: One should also command Yang Province to select a fierce general and dispatch that province's troops to Fushan, attacking from both outside and inside in a pincer."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Province should also be ordered to choose a fierce general and send its local troops to Fushan, so that inner and outer forces may strike together.

sentences.zh: 朝議從之。

translations.literal: The court deliberation accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his plan.

sentences.zh: 出除使持節、散騎常侍、都督雍岐華三州諸軍事、征西將軍、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: He was dispatched and appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs in the three provinces of Yong, Qi, and Hua, General Who Pacifies the West, and Governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out and appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs in Yong, Qi, and Hua, General Who Pacifies the West, and Governor of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 太和以前，朝法尤峻，貴臣蹉跌，便致誅夷。

translations.literal: Before the Taihe era, court law was especially severe; when high ministers stumbled, execution immediately followed.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Taihe era, court law was especially harsh: when great ministers slipped, they were cut down at once.

sentences.zh: 李沖之用事也，欽祚識幹，薦為左丞，又兼黃門。

translations.literal: When Li Chong was in power, appreciating Zuo's talent and capability, he recommended him as Left Assistant [Director], and additionally made him concurrent Superintendent of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Chong held power, he recognized Zuo's talent and ability, recommended him as Left Assistant Director, and also gave him the concurrent post of Superintendent of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 意便滿足，每以孤門往經崔氏之禍，常慮危亡，苦自陳挹，辭色懇然，發於誠至。

translations.literal: He was then content in mind; yet because as a lone family they had previously suffered the disaster of the Cui clan, he constantly feared ruin and death, painfully humbled himself in self-deprecation, his words and expression earnest, arising from genuine sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: He was satisfied at heart, yet as a lone house that had once been swept up in the Cui clan's ruin, he lived in constant fear of destruction. He humbled himself again and again, his words and bearing painfully earnest, born of true sincerity.

sentences.zh: 沖謂之曰：「人生有運，非可避也，但當明白當官，何所顧畏。」

translations.literal: Li Chong said to him: "Human life has its fate, which cannot be avoided; one need only serve one's office with integrity—what is there to fear?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong told him, "Life has its allotted course, and there is no escaping it. Serve your office with a clear conscience—what is there to fear?

sentences.zh: 自是積二十餘年，位秩隆重，而進趨之心更復不息。

translations.literal: From then on, for more than twenty years, his rank and position were grand and lofty, yet his ambition to advance never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, for more than twenty years, his rank and honors grew ever grander, yet his hunger for advancement never slackened.

sentences.zh: 又以東宮師傅之資，列辭尚書，志在封侯、儀同之位，尚書令、任城王澄為之奏聞。

translations.literal: Also relying on his credentials as tutor of the Eastern Palace, he repeatedly submitted memorials to the Ministry of Works, aiming for the rank of marquis and the status of Three Excellencies Equaling the Imperial Son-in-Law; Director of the Ministry of Works, Prince Cheng of Ren, memorialized on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Leaning on his standing as tutor of the Eastern Palace, he repeatedly petitioned the Ministry of Works, seeking a marquisate and the rank of Palace Attendant. The Minister of Works, Prince Cheng of Ren, submitted the request on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 及為征西、雍州，雖喜於外撫，尚以府號不優，心望加大，執政者頗怪之。

translations.literal: When he became General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Yong, though he was pleased to govern externally, he still regarded his title as insufficiently distinguished and inwardly hoped for greater honors; those in power were rather displeased by this.
translations.idiomatic: When he became General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Yong, he was glad to govern in the provinces, yet still felt his title too modest and inwardly hoped for greater rank. Those in power were displeased.

sentences.zh: 於時，領軍于忠恃寵驕恣，崔光之徒，曲躬承奉，祚心惡之，乃遣子太尉從事中郎景尚說高陽王雍，令出忠為州。

translations.literal: At that time, the Director of the Imperial Guards Yu Zhong relied on favor and was arrogant and willful; Cui Guang and his kind bowed and slavishly flattered him. Zuo detested this in his heart and sent his son Jing Shang, Attendant Gentleman of the Grand Commandant's Staff, to persuade Prince Yong of Gaoyang to have Yu Zhong sent out to govern a province.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Director of the Imperial Guards, Yu Zhong, rode on imperial favor and grew arrogant and unrestrained; Cui Guang and men like him bowed low to court him. Zuo hated this and sent his son Jing Shang, Attendant Gentleman on the Grand Commandant's staff, to persuade Prince Yong of Gaoyang to have Yu Zhong posted out to a provincial command.

sentences.zh: 忠聞而大怒，矯詔殺祚，時年六十七。

translations.literal: Yu Zhong heard of this and was greatly enraged; he forged an imperial edict and had Zuo killed. He was sixty-seven years old at the time.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Zhong heard of it, he flew into a rage, forged an imperial edict, and had Zuo killed. Zuo was sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 祚達於政事，凡所經履，咸為稱職，每有斷決，多為故事。

translations.literal: Zuo was accomplished in state affairs; whatever posts he passed through, all were regarded as fitting the role; whenever he made decisions, many became precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo was skilled in governance. Every office he held, he filled competently; many of his rulings became precedents.

sentences.zh: 名器既重，時望亦深，一朝非罪見害，遠近莫不惋惜。

translations.literal: His official honors were already weighty and contemporary esteem for him was also deep; in a single morning he was harmed without crime, and near and far none failed to lament.
translations.idiomatic: His rank was already great and his reputation deep; when he was destroyed without cause in a single morning, men near and far mourned him.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，遣使弔慰，追復伯爵。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling assumed the regency, she sent envoys to offer condolences, and posthumously restored his marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling took the regency, she sent envoys to offer condolences and posthumously restored his marquisate.

sentences.zh: 正光中，贈使持節、車騎將軍、儀同三司、雍州刺史，諡文貞公。

translations.literal: During the Zhengguang era, he was posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Three Excellencies Equaling the Imperial Son-in-Law, and Governor of Yong Province, with the posthumous title Duke Wen Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengguang era he was posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Palace Attendant, and Governor of Yong Province, with the posthumous title Duke Wen Zhen.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖之置中正，從容謂祚曰：「并州中正，卿家故應推王瓊也。」

translations.literal: Initially, when Emperor Gaozu established the zhongzheng system, he casually said to Zuo: "For Bingzhou zhongzheng, your family should originally have recommended Wang Qiong."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Wen established the zhongzheng system, he said casually to Zuo, "For Bingzhou's zhongzheng, your family ought to have recommended Wang Qiong.

sentences.zh: 祚退謂密友曰：「瓊真偽今自未辨，我家何為減之？

translations.literal: Zuo withdrew and said to a close friend: "Whether Qiong is genuine or false has not yet been determined—why should our family be diminished?
translations.idiomatic: When Zuo withdrew, he told a close friend, "Whether Qiong is genuine or false is still unclear—why should our house be reduced?

sentences.zh: 然主上直信李沖吹噓之說耳。」

translations.literal: Yet the sovereign simply believes Li Chong's boasting claims, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor simply believes whatever Li Chong boasts, that is all.

sentences.zh: 祚死後三歲而于忠死，咸以祚為祟。

translations.literal: Three years after Zuo's death, Yu Zhong died; all believed Zuo's spirit was responsible.
translations.idiomatic: Three years after Zuo's death Yu Zhong died, and all believed Zuo's ghost had brought it about.

sentences.zh: 祚長子思恭，弱冠，州辟為主簿。

translations.literal: Zuo's eldest son Sigong, upon reaching adulthood, was recruited by the province as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo's eldest son Sigong, upon coming of age, was recruited by the province as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died early.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 思恭弟慶禮以第二子延伯繼。

translations.literal: Sigong's younger brother Qingli had his second son Yanbo succeed [to the line].
translations.idiomatic: Sigong's younger brother Qingli had his second son Yanbo succeed to the line.

sentences.zh: 延伯，襲祖爵東光伯。

translations.literal: Yanbo inherited his grandfather's title, Marquis of Dongguang.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo inherited his grandfather's title, Marquis of Dongguang.

sentences.zh: 武定中，驃騎大將軍、將作大匠。

translations.literal: During the Wuding era, [he served as] General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wuding era he served as General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master of Works.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication [of Wei], his title was reduced according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, his title was reduced according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 思恭弟景尚，字思和。

translations.literal: Sigong's younger brother Jing Shang, courtesy name Sihe.
translations.idiomatic: Sigong's younger brother Jing Shang, courtesy name Sihe.

sentences.zh: 涉歷書傳，曉星歷占候，言事頗驗。

translations.literal: He ranged widely through books and classics, understood astrology and divination, and his prognostications on affairs were largely borne out.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely in the classics, understood the stars, calendrics, and divination, and his predictions about affairs often proved true.

sentences.zh: 初為彭城王中軍府參軍，遷員外郎、司徒主簿、太尉從事中郎。

translations.literal: Initially he served as aide in the Prince of Pengcheng's Central Army Office; he was promoted to supplementary gentleman, chief clerk of the Minister of Public Works, and Attendant Gentleman on the Grand Commandant's staff.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as aide in the Prince of Pengcheng's Central Army Office, then rose to supplementary gentleman, chief clerk of the Minister of Public Works, and Attendant Gentleman on the Grand Commandant's staff.

sentences.zh: 公強當世，善事權寵，世號之曰「郭尖」。

translations.literal: He was forceful and dominating in his age, skilled at cultivating power and favor; contemporaries called him "Guo the Sharp Point."
translations.idiomatic: Forceful and dominant in his day, he was skilled at courting power and favor; his contemporaries called him "Sharp Guo."

sentences.zh: 肅宗時，遷輔國將軍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: During Emperor Suzong's reign, he was promoted to General Who Supports the State and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Suzong he was promoted to General Who Supports the State and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 轉中書侍郎，未拜而卒，年五十一。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat but died before taking office; he was fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat but died before assuming the post, at the age of fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 子季方，武定中，膠州驃騎府長流參軍。

translations.literal: His son Jifang, during the Wuding era, served as senior administrative aide in the Agile Cavalry office of Jiao Province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jifang, in the Wuding era, served as senior administrative aide in the Agile Cavalry office of Jiao Province.

sentences.zh: 景尚弟慶禮，字叔，為祚所愛。

translations.literal: Jing Shang's younger brother Qingli, courtesy name Shu, was beloved by Zuo.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Shang's younger brother Qingli, courtesy name Shu, was a favorite of Zuo's.

sentences.zh: 著作佐郎、通直郎。

translations.literal: [He served as] Assistant Gentleman of Composition and Direct Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Assistant Gentleman of Composition and Direct Attendant.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈征虜將軍、瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: Upon his death, he was posthumously granted the title General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Governor of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously granted the title General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Governor of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 子元貞，武定末，定州驃騎府長史。

translations.literal: His son Yuanzhen, at the end of the Wuding era, served as chief administrator in the Agile Cavalry office of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanzhen, at the end of the Wuding era, served as chief administrator in the Agile Cavalry office of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 張彝，字慶賓，清河東武城人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi, courtesy name Qingbin, was a native of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi, courtesy name Qingbin, was a native of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 曾祖幸，慕容超東牟太守，後率戶歸國。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xing was Administrator of Dongmu under Murong Chao; afterward he led his household to surrender to [Northern Wei].
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xing had been Administrator of Dongmu under Murong Chao; later he led his household in submission to the Wei.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘉之，賜爵平陸侯，拜平遠將軍、青州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu commended him, bestowed the title Marquis of Pinglu, and appointed him General of Pacifying the Distance and Governor of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu praised him, granted him the title Marquis of Pinglu, and appointed him General of Pacifying the Distance and Governor of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 祖準之襲，又為東青州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhun inherited [the title] and also served as Governor of Eastern Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhun inherited the title and also served as Governor of Eastern Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 父靈真，早卒。

translations.literal: His father Lingzhen died early.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lingzhen died young.

sentences.zh: 彝性公強，有風氣，歷覽經史。

translations.literal: Yi was by nature forthright and forceful, possessed moral stature, and read widely in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was by nature upright and forceful, possessed of moral bearing, and had read widely in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，襲祖侯爵，與盧淵、李安民等結為親友，往來朝會，常相追隨。

translations.literal: In the early years of Emperor Gaozu, he inherited his grandfather's marquisate and formed friendships with Lu Yuan, Li Anmin, and others; at court gatherings they were often in each other's company.
translations.idiomatic: In the early years of Emperor Wen, he inherited his grandfather's marquisate and became close friends with Lu Yuan, Li Anmin, and others; at court they were often together.

sentences.zh: 淵為主客令，安民與彝並為散令。

translations.literal: Yuan was Director of Guests; Anmin and Yi were both Directors of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yuan was Director of Guests; Li Anmin and Zhang Yi were both Directors of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 彝少而豪放，出入殿庭，步眄高上，無所顧忌。

translations.literal: Yi from youth was bold and unrestrained; entering and leaving the palace hall, he walked with his gaze lifted high, without any restraint.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Zhang Yi was bold and free-spirited; entering and leaving the palace halls, he walked with his eyes lifted high, heedless of restraint.

sentences.zh: 文明太后雅尚恭謹，因會次見其如此，遂召集百僚督責之，令其修悔，而猶無悛改。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming greatly valued reverence and prudence; on one occasion at court she saw him behave thus, whereupon she assembled the hundred officials to supervise and rebuke him, ordering him to repent and reform—yet he still showed no change of heart.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming prized reverence and restraint. Once at court she saw him behave so and summoned the hundred officials to rebuke him publicly, ordering him to repent—but he still would not change.

sentences.zh: 善於督察，每東西馳使有所巡檢，彝恒充其選，清慎嚴猛，所至人皆畏伏，儔類亦以此高之。

translations.literal: He was skilled at supervision and inspection; whenever emissaries were dispatched east and west for inspections, Yi was invariably chosen; clear, cautious, strict, and severe—wherever he went people feared and submitted, and his peers also held him in high regard for this.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at inspection. Whenever envoys were sent east or west on tour, Yi was always chosen. Clear, cautious, strict, and stern, he inspired fear wherever he went, and his peers respected him for it.

sentences.zh: 遷主客令，例降侯為伯，轉太中大夫，仍行主客曹事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of Guests; by regulation his marquisate was reduced to a viscountcy; he was transferred to Grand Palace Grandee and continued to handle the affairs of the Bureau of Guests.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of Guests; by regulation his marquisate was reduced to a viscountcy. He became Grand Palace Grandee and continued to handle the Bureau of Guests.

sentences.zh: 尋為黃門。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he became Superintendent of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made Superintendent of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 後從駕南征，母憂解任。

translations.literal: Later he accompanied the emperor on the southern campaign and resigned his post upon his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: Later he accompanied the emperor on the southern campaign, then left office upon his mother's death.

sentences.zh: 彝居喪過禮，送葬自平城達家，千里徒步，不乘車馬，顏貌毀瘠，當世稱之。

translations.literal: Yi observed mourning beyond the prescribed rites; to escort the funeral from Pingcheng to his home he walked a thousand li on foot without riding horse or carriage; his appearance was gaunt and wasted—the age praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi mourned beyond the prescribed rites. To escort the funeral from Pingcheng home—a thousand li—he went entirely on foot, never mounting horse or carriage. His face was wasted and gaunt, and his age praised him.

sentences.zh: 高祖幸冀州，遣使弔慰，詔以驍騎將軍起之，還復本位。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu visited Ji Province, sent envoys to offer condolences, and ordered him recalled as General of Valiant Cavalry; upon return he resumed his former position.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen visited Ji Province, he sent envoys to offer condolences and ordered Zhang Yi recalled as General of Valiant Cavalry. On his return he resumed his former post.

sentences.zh: 以參定遷都之勳，進爵為侯，轉太常少卿，遷散騎常侍，兼侍中，持節巡察陝東、河南十二州，甚有聲稱。

translations.literal: For his merit in participating in deciding the capital relocation, he was advanced to marquis, transferred to Vice Director of the Grand Imperial Ancestral Temple, promoted to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and concurrently Palace Attendant, bearing the staff to inspect the twelve provinces of Shaan East and Henan—his reputation was greatly enhanced.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit in planning the move of the capital, he was raised to marquis, made Vice Director of the Grand Imperial Ancestral Temple, then Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and concurrent Palace Attendant, bearing the staff to inspect the twelve provinces of Shaan East and Henan. His reputation soared.

sentences.zh: 使還，以從征之勤，遷尚書。

translations.literal: Upon returning from his mission, for his diligence on the campaign he was promoted to Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned from his mission, he was promoted to Director of the Ministry of Works for his service on campaign.

sentences.zh: 坐舉元昭為兼郎中，黜為守尚書。

translations.literal: He was demoted to Acting Director of the Ministry of Works for having recommended Yuan Zhao as concurrent Gentleman in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to Acting Director of the Ministry of Works for recommending Yuan Zhao as concurrent Gentleman in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，除正尚書、兼侍中，尋正侍中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign, he was appointed full Director of the Ministry of Works and concurrent Palace Attendant; shortly afterward he became full Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was made full Director of the Ministry of Works and concurrent Palace Attendant, and soon afterward full Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 世宗親政，罷六輔，彝與兼尚書邢巒聞處分非常，出京奔走，為御史中尉甄琛所彈，云「非虎非兕，率彼曠野」，詔書切責之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong personally assumed government and dismissed the Six Assistants, Yi and Vice Director Xing Luan, hearing that the measures were extraordinary, fled the capital; they were impeached by the Inspector-in-Chief Zhen Chen, citing "Neither tiger nor rhinoceros—driving through the open wild," and an imperial edict sternly rebuked them.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu took personal rule and dismissed the Six Assistants, Zhang Yi and Vice Director Xing Luan, hearing that extraordinary measures were afoot, fled the capital. Inspector-in-Chief Zhen Chen impeached them with the line "Neither tiger nor rhinoceros—driving through the open wild," and an imperial edict sharply rebuked them.

sentences.zh: 尋除安西將軍、秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 彝務尚典式，考訪故事。

translations.literal: Yi devoted himself to institutional forms and investigated precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi devoted himself to proper forms and searched out precedent.

sentences.zh: 及臨隴右，彌加討習，於是出入直衞，方伯威儀，赫然可觀。

translations.literal: When he arrived in Longyou [the west], he applied himself all the more to study and practice; thus whether entering or leaving, his imperial guard escort and the majesty of a regional governor were visibly imposing.
translations.idiomatic: When he took up his post in Longyou, he applied himself all the more to study and drill. Whether entering or leaving, his guard escort and the bearing of a frontier governor were visibly imposing.

sentences.zh: 羌夏畏伏，憚其威整，一方肅靜，號為良牧。

translations.literal: The Qiang and Xia peoples feared and submitted, dreading his stern authority; the region was tranquil and he was hailed as an excellent governor.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang and Xia submitted in fear of his stern discipline. The region grew quiet, and he was hailed as an excellent governor.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，太極初就，彝與郭祚等俱以勤舊被徵。

translations.literal: That winter, when the Taiji Palace was first completed, Yi and Guo Zuo and others were all summoned for their long service and seniority.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when the Taiji Palace was first completed, Zhang Yi and Guo Zuo and others were all summoned to court for their long service.

sentences.zh: 及還州，進號撫軍將軍，彝表解州任，詔不許。

translations.literal: When he returned to his province, his title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the Army; Yi submitted a memorial requesting to relinquish his provincial post, but the edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to his province his title was raised to General Who Pacifies the Army. Zhang Yi memorialized asking to resign the governorship, but the edict refused.

sentences.zh: 彝敷政隴右，多所制立，宣布新風，革其舊俗，民庶愛仰之。

translations.literal: Yi spread good governance in Longyou, establishing many new regulations, proclaiming a new ethos and reforming old customs; the people loved and admired him.
translations.idiomatic: In Longyou Zhang Yi governed broadly, establishing many new rules, proclaiming a new ethos and reforming old custom. The people loved and looked up to him.

sentences.zh: 為國造佛寺名曰興皇，諸有罪咎者，隨其輕重，謫為土木之功，無復鞭杖之罰。

translations.literal: He built for the state a Buddhist temple named Xinghuang; all who had offenses were, according to severity, relegated to labor on construction works, with no further flogging punishments.
translations.idiomatic: For the state he built a Buddhist temple called Xinghuang. Offenders, according to the weight of their crimes, were assigned to construction labor instead of being flogged.

sentences.zh: 時陳留公主寡居，彝意願尚主，主亦許之。

translations.literal: At that time the Princess of Chenliu was widowed; Yi wished to marry her, and the princess also agreed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Princess of Chenliu was a widow. Zhang Yi wished to marry her, and the princess agreed.

sentences.zh: 僕射高肇亦望尚主，主意不可。

translations.literal: Vice Director Gao Zhao also hoped to marry the princess, but the princess would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Gao Zhao also hoped to marry her, but the princess would not have it.

sentences.zh: 肇怒，譖彝於世宗，稱彝擅立刑法，勞役百姓。

translations.literal: Gao Zhao was enraged and slandered Yi to Emperor Shizong, claiming Yi had arbitrarily established penal laws and conscripted the people in labor.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhao was furious and slandered Zhang Yi to Emperor Xuanwu, saying he had set up punishments on his own authority and overworked the people.

sentences.zh: 詔遣直後萬貳興馳驛撿察。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched the Direct Attendant Wan Erxing post-haste by relay to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Direct Attendant Wan Erxing post-haste by relay to investigate.

sentences.zh: 貳興，肇所親愛，必欲致彝深罪。

translations.literal: Erxing was a man Gao Zhao cherished and favored; he was determined to bring deep guilt upon Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Erxing was a man Gao Zhao favored and was bent on bringing Zhang Yi to ruin.

sentences.zh: 彝清身奉法，求其愆過，遂無所得。

translations.literal: Yi had kept himself pure and upheld the law; they sought his faults and ultimately found nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi had kept himself clean and upheld the law; they searched for fault and found none.

sentences.zh: 見代還洛，猶停廢數年，因得偏風，手脚不便。

translations.literal: When his replacement arrived he returned to Luoyang, yet remained idle and dismissed for several years; he thereupon contracted hemiplegia and his hands and feet were impaired.
translations.idiomatic: When his successor arrived he returned to Luoyang, but remained idle for several years. He then suffered a stroke and his hands and feet were impaired.

sentences.zh: 然志性不移，善自將攝，稍能朝拜。

translations.literal: Yet his will and character did not change; he was good at caring for himself and gradually was able to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his spirit did not change. He cared for himself well and gradually was able to attend court again.

sentences.zh: 久之，除光祿大夫，加金章紫綬。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the gold seal and purple sash.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the gold seal and purple sash.

sentences.zh: 彝愛好知己，輕忽下流，非其意者，視之蔑爾。

translations.literal: Yi loved and favored those he knew well and slighted those of lower rank; those who did not suit his liking he regarded with contempt.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi cherished those he knew and looked down on those beneath him; anyone who did not suit him he treated with contempt.

sentences.zh: 雖疹疾家庭，而志氣彌亮。

translations.literal: Though afflicted with illness at home, his spirit was all the brighter.
translations.idiomatic: Though illness kept him at home, his resolve burned all the brighter.

sentences.zh: 上表曰：「臣聞元天高朗，尚假列星以助明；

translations.literal: In a memorial he said: "Your servant has heard that though the primordial Heaven is lofty and clear, it still borrows the array of stars to aid its brilliance;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the throne: "I have heard that though primordial Heaven is high and clear, it still borrows the array of stars to help its light;

sentences.zh: 洞庭淵湛，猶藉眾流以增大。

translations.literal: though Dongting is deep and vast, it still relies on many streams to enlarge it.
translations.idiomatic: though Dongting is deep and vast, it still relies on many streams to swell its breadth.

sentences.zh: 莫不以孤照不詣其幽，獨深未盡其廣。

translations.literal: None can illuminate the hidden with a solitary beam, nor exhaust the breadth with depth alone.
translations.idiomatic: Neither solitary light reaches every shadow, nor solitary depth fills every expanse.

sentences.zh: 先聖識其若此，必取物以自誡。

translations.literal: The ancient sages, knowing this to be so, invariably took material things as admonitions to themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient sages, knowing this, always took things around them as warnings to themselves.

sentences.zh: 故堯稱則天，設謗木以曉未明；

translations.literal: Thus Yao, styled "the Pattern of Heaven," set up a wooden board for criticism to make known what was unclear;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Yao, styled Pattern of Heaven, set up a board for criticism to reveal what was still dark;

sentences.zh: 舜稱盡善，懸諫鼓以規政闕。

translations.literal: Shun, styled "Utmost Goodness," hung a remonstrance drum to mark flaws in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Shun, styled Utmost Goodness, hung a drum for remonstrance to mark what was lacking in government.

sentences.zh: 虞人獻箴規之旨，盤盂著舉動之銘，庶幾見善而思齊，聞惡以自改。

translations.literal: Forest keepers offered the purpose of admonition and regulation; basins and cups bore inscriptions on conduct—so that upon seeing good one might aspire to emulate it, and upon hearing evil one might reform oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Forest keepers offered words of admonition; basins and cups bore inscriptions on conduct—so that seeing good one would strive to match it, and hearing evil one would turn and reform.

sentences.zh: 眷眷於悔往之衢，孜孜於不逮之路，用能聲高百王，卓絕中古，經十氏而不渝，歷二千以孤鬱。

translations.literal: Attentive on the path of repenting past errors, diligent on the road of what one has not yet attained—thus their fame towered above the hundred kings, transcendent through the middle antiquity, enduring through ten dynasties without change, spanning two thousand years in solitary eminence.
translations.idiomatic: Attentive on the road of repenting the past, tireless on the path of what they had not yet reached—they raised their fame above the hundred kings, stood alone through the middle ages, endured through ten houses without wavering, and shone across two thousand years.

sentences.zh: 伏惟太祖撥亂，弈代重光。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Grand Ancestor [Emperor Taiwu] quelled the chaos, and generation after generation renewed the imperial splendor.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Grand Ancestor quelled the chaos, and dynasty after dynasty renewed the imperial light.

sentences.zh: 世祖以不世之才，開盪函夏；

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu, with matchless talent, opened and swept across the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu, possessing extraordinary talent, expanded rule over the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 顯祖以溫明之德，潤沃九區。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzu, with warm and bright virtue, moistened and enriched the nine regions.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzu, with his gentle and luminous virtue, nourished all the realm.

sentences.zh: [2]高祖大聖臨朝，經營云始，未明求衣，日昃忘食，開翦荊棘，徙御神縣，更新風軌，冠帶朝流。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu the great sage attended court, beginning his efforts at the start; rising before daylight and forgetting to eat at sunset, he cleared thorns and brambles, moved the capital to the sacred heartland, renewed customs and institutions, and drew the girdled and capped to court.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu the great sage came to the throne and began his labors from the very start—rising before dawn and forgetting meals at dusk—cutting away brambles, moving the capital to the sacred heartland, renewing laws and customs, and drawing the civilized world to court.

sentences.zh: 海東雜種之渠，衡南異服之帥，沙西氊頭之戎，漠北辮髮之虜，重譯納貢，請吏稱藩。

translations.literal: Chiefs of mixed tribes east of the sea, chieftains in strange dress south of Heng, felt-hatted barbarians west of the sands, and braided-haired enemies north of the desert—all came through multiple translations to offer tribute and requested officials, styling themselves as vassals.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal leaders from the eastern seas, southern chiefs in exotic dress, felt-hatted barbarians west of the sands, and braided-haired peoples north of the desert—all sent tribute through successive interpreters and requested imperial administrators, styling themselves as vassals.

sentences.zh: 積德懋於夏殷，富仁盛於周漢，澤教既周，武功亦匝。

translations.literal: Accumulated virtue surpassing Xia and Yin, abundant benevolence exceeding Zhou and Han—benevolent instruction was complete, and martial achievements likewise comprehensive.
translations.idiomatic: Their accumulated virtue surpassed that of the Xia and Shang, their benevolence exceeded that of the Zhou and Han; civilizing influence was complete, and military achievements likewise comprehensive.

sentences.zh: 猶且發明詔，思求直士，信是蒼生薦言之秋，祝史陳辭之日。

translations.literal: Moreover they issued bright edicts seeking upright men—it was truly the season for the common people to offer advice and for the prayer-officers to present their words.
translations.idiomatic: They even issued enlightened decrees seeking upright officials—it was truly the season when the people might offer counsel and when the ritual officials might speak their minds.

sentences.zh: 況臣家自奉國八十餘年，紆金鏘玉，及臣四世。

translations.literal: Moreover, my family has served the state for over eighty years, adorned with gold seals and jade insignia, extending to four generations including myself.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, my family has served the state for over eighty years, honored with gold seals and jade insignia, spanning four generations down to me.

sentences.zh: 過以小才，藉蔭出仕，學慚專門，武闕方略，早荷先帝眷仗之恩，末蒙陛下不遺之施。

translations.literal: I overstepped with my small talent, entered office through inherited favor; ashamed in learning for lacking specialization and in warfare for lacking strategy—I early received the previous emperor's trusting favor and finally Your Majesty's gracious consideration without abandonment.
translations.idiomatic: I came to office beyond my modest abilities through inherited privilege; I lacked specialized learning and military strategy. I was early favored by the late emperor and later found favor with Your Majesty despite my unworthiness.

sentences.zh: [3]侍則出入兩都，[4]官歷納言常伯，忝牧秦藩，號兼安撫。

translations.literal: Attending at court I moved between the two capitals; my offices included Chief Counselor and Regular Grandee, and I shamefully governed the Qin domain with the concurrent title of Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: I attended at court, moving between the two capitals; I served as Chief Counselor and Regular Grandee, and shamefully governed the Qin domain with the concurrent title of Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 實思碎首膏原，仰酬二朝之惠；

translations.literal: Truly I wished to smash my head and smear my blood on the plain, looking up to repay the grace of two reigns.
translations.idiomatic: I truly wished to give my life to repay the kindness of two emperors.

sentences.zh: 輕塵碎石，遠增嵩岱之高。

translations.literal: Light as dust and broken stone, I hoped from afar to increase the height of Mount Song and Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Though insignificant as dust or pebbles, I hoped from afar to add to the stature of Mount Song and Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 輒私訪舊書，竊觀圖史，其帝皇興起之元，配天隆家之業，修造益民之奇，龍麟雲鳳之瑞，卑宮愛物之仁，釋網改祝之澤，前歌後舞之應，囹圄寂寥之美，可為輝風景行者，輒謹編丹青，以標睿範。

translations.literal: I then privately consulted old books and secretly viewed illustrated histories; of emperors' rise to power, enterprises matching Heaven and elevating families, marvelous works benefiting the people, auspicious signs of dragons, qilin, clouds, and phoenixes, the benevolence of humble palaces and love of creatures, the grace of releasing nets and changing prayers, the response of singing before and dancing behind, and the beauty of empty prisons—all that could illuminate and inspire—I carefully compiled in paintings to mark the wise standard.
