translations.idiomatic: I privately consulted ancient texts and historical records, and for accounts of emperors' founding achievements, dynastic glory endorsed by Heaven, marvelous works benefiting the people, auspicious omens of dragons, qilin, clouds, and phoenixes, humane governance through frugal palaces and care for creatures, merciful policies of sparing the net and reforming sacrifices, popular rejoicing, and the virtue of empty prisons—all that could inspire and instruct—I carefully compiled them in illustrated form to mark the wise standard.

sentences.zh: 至如太康好田，遇窮后迫禍；

translations.literal: King Taikang loved hunting and met disaster when the end came and his empress brought ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Taikang loved hunting and met disaster when the end came and his empress brought ruin.

sentences.zh: 武乙逸禽，罹震雷暴酷；

translations.literal: King Wuyi amused himself with flying birds and suffered violent thunder in punishment.
translations.idiomatic: King Wuyi amused himself with flying birds and was struck down by thunder in violent punishment.

sentences.zh: 夏桀淫亂，南巢有非命之誅；

translations.literal: Xia Jie was licentious and disorderly; at Nanqiao there was execution not by fate.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Jie was debauched and tyrannical; at Nanqiao he met an untimely death.

sentences.zh: 殷紂昏酣，牧野有倒戈之陳；

translations.literal: King Zhou of Yin was muddled and drunken; at Muye there was the array of turned spears.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhou of Yin was dissolute and drunk; at Muye his troops turned their weapons against him.

sentences.zh: 周厲逐獸，滅不旋踵；

translations.literal: King Li of Zhou chased beasts; destruction came without turning the heel.
translations.idiomatic: King Li of Zhou obsessed over hunting; his ruin followed almost immediately.

sentences.zh: 幽王遇惑，死亦相尋；

translations.literal: King You met deception; death followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: King You was beguiled into error; death soon followed in turn.

sentences.zh: 暨於漢成失御，亡新篡奪；

translations.literal: Later came Han Chengdi's loss of control and Wang Mang's usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: Later came Han Chengdi's loss of control and Wang Mang's usurpation.

sentences.zh: 桓靈不綱，魏武遷鼎；

translations.literal: Emperors Huan and Ling lacked discipline; Cao Cao moved the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Huan and Ling neglected governance; Cao Cao moved the imperial seat.

sentences.zh: 晉惠闇弱，骨肉相屠，終使聰曜鴞視并州，勒虎狼據燕趙：如此之輩，罔不畢載。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui of Jin was dim and weak; kin slaughtered one another, ultimately allowing Liu Cong and Liu Yao to owl-watch Bingzhou and Shi Le to wolf-like occupy Yan and Zhao—all such types are without exception fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui of Jin was weak and muddled; his kin slaughtered one another, ultimately allowing Liu Cong and Liu Yao to covet Bingzhou like owls and Shi Le to wolf-like occupy Yan and Zhao—all such cases are fully recorded.

sentences.zh: 起元庖犧，終於晉末，凡十六代，百二十八帝，歷三千二百七年，雜事五百八十九，合成五卷，名曰歷帝圖，亦謗木、諫鼓、虞人、盤盂之類。

translations.literal: Beginning from Fuxi at the origin and ending at the end of Jin—in all sixteen dynasties, 128 emperors, spanning 3,207 years, with 589 miscellaneous matters—compiled into five volumes titled Chronicle of Emperors, akin to remonstrance boards, advice drums, forest keepers, and inscribed basins of old.
translations.idiomatic: From Fuxi at the beginning to the end of Jin—sixteen dynasties, 128 emperors, 3,207 years, and 589 miscellaneous records—compiled into five volumes titled Chronicle of Emperors, akin to the remonstrance boards, advice drums, forest keepers, and inscribed basins of old.

sentences.zh: 脫蒙置御坐之側，時復披覽，冀或起予左右，上補未萌。

translations.literal: If I am fortunate enough to have it placed beside the imperial seat for occasional reading, I hope it may occasionally awaken me at your side and help remedy troubles before they arise.
translations.idiomatic: If it might be placed beside Your Majesty's seat for occasional reading, I hope it may occasionally awaken me at your side and help remedy troubles before they arise.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下遠惟宗廟之憂，近存黎民之念，取其賢君，棄其惡主，則微臣雖沉淪地下，無異乘雲登天矣。」

translations.literal: I humbly wish Your Majesty would far consider the ancestors' concerns and near preserve thoughts of the people, taking the worthy rulers and discarding the evil ones—then though I sink underground, it would be no different from riding clouds to ascend heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray Your Majesty will heed distant concerns for the ancestral temple and keep near in mind the welfare of the people, taking the worthy rulers as models and rejecting the wicked—then though I lie buried underground, it would be as if I ascended to heaven on clouds.

sentences.zh: 世宗善之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu approved it.

sentences.zh: 彝又表曰：「竊惟皇王統天，必以窮幽為美；

translations.literal: Zhang Yi again memorialized: "I reflect that emperors and kings who harmonize with Heaven must take penetrating the obscure as excellence;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi submitted another memorial: "I believe that emperors who align with Heaven must regard penetrating the hidden as a virtue;

sentences.zh: 盡理作聖，亦假廣採成明。

translations.literal: To exhaust principle and become sage likewise borrows broad collection to achieve clarity.
translations.idiomatic: To perfect understanding and become sage likewise depends on broad collection to achieve enlightenment.

sentences.zh: 故詢於芻蕘，著之周什，輿人獻箴，流於夏典。

translations.literal: Therefore inquiry was made of grass cutters, recorded in the Odes of Zhou; chariot makers presented admonitions, flowing into the canon of Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Hence inquiry was made even of grass cutters and recorded in the Zhou odes, and chariot makers offered admonitions preserved in the Xia canon.

sentences.zh: 不然，則美刺無以得彰，善惡有時不達。

translations.literal: Otherwise, praise and censure could not be made manifest, and good and evil would at times fail to reach [the throne].
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise praise and blame could never be made clear, and good and evil would sometimes never reach the ruler.

sentences.zh: 逮於兩漢、魏、晉，雖道有隆汚，而被繡傳檄，未始闕也。

translations.literal: Reaching the Two Han, Wei, and Jin—though the Way had ascent and defilement—embroidered robes conveying memorials never once were lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Down through the Two Han, Wei, and Jin, though governance rose and fell, officials in court dress presenting memorials never ceased.

sentences.zh: 及惠帝失御，中夏崩離，劉苻專據秦西，燕趙獨制關左，姚夏繼起，五涼競立，致使九服搖搖，民無定主，禮儀典制，此焉堙滅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui lost control, the Central Plains collapsed and split apart; Liu and Fu monopolized western Qin, Yan and Zhao alone controlled the passes to the left, Yao of Xia rose in succession, and the Five Liang competed to establish themselves—causing the nine domains to sway unsteadily, the people without a fixed lord, and ritual codes and institutions to be buried and extinguished here.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Hui lost the throne, the heartland fragmented; Liu and Fu held western Qin, Yan and Zhao controlled the eastern passes, Later Yan and the Five Liang rose in turn—the nine provinces trembled, the people had no settled ruler, and ritual and institutions perished.

sentences.zh: 暨大魏應歷，撥亂登皇，翦彼鯨鯢，龕靖神縣，數紀之間，天下寧一，傳輝七帝，積聖如神。

translations.literal: When Great Wei received the mandate, quelling chaos and ascending the throne, cutting down those whale-demons and peacefully settling the divine counties, within a few reigns the realm was united under one rule, transmitting glory through seven emperors, accumulated sagacity like a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Wei received the mandate, quelled chaos, and took the throne, it cut down its foes and restored order to the realm; within a few reigns the empire was unified, seven emperors passed down its glory, and sagacity accumulated like that of a spirit.

sentences.zh: 高祖遷鼎成周，永茲八百，偃武修文，憲章斯改，實所謂加五帝、登三王，民無德而名焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu moved the tripod to Cheng and Zhou, continuing those eight hundred years, laying down arms and cultivating culture, statutes and patterns thereby reformed—truly what is called surpassing the Five Emperors and ascending the Three Kings, the people without virtue yet naming it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu moved the capital to Luoyang, continuing the Zhou legacy of eight hundred years, sheathed the sword and fostered letters, and reformed law and institutions—truly surpassing the Five Emperors and equaling the Three Kings, a fame the people need not ascribe to virtue alone.

sentences.zh: 猶且慮獨見之不明，欲廣訪於得失，乃命四使，觀察風謠。

translations.literal: Yet he still worried that solitary insight was not clear, and wished broadly to inquire into gains and losses; therefore he ordered four envoys to observe popular songs and rumors.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he still feared that his own judgment alone might be unclear and wished to seek widely for what was right and wrong; he therefore appointed four envoys to observe folk songs and local opinion.

sentences.zh: 臣時忝常伯，充一使之列，遂得仗節揮金，宣恩東夏，周歷於齊魯之間，遍馳於梁宋之域，詢採詩頌，研撿獄情，實庶片言之不遺，美刺之俱顯。

translations.literal: Your subject at the time held the post of Regular Grandee and filled one place among the envoys; thus I was able to bear the staff and wield gold, proclaiming grace in eastern Xia, touring between Qi and Lu, ranging widely through the lands of Liang and Song, inquiring into and collecting odes and hymns, examining and sorting prison cases—truly hoping that not a single word would be lost and that praise and censure alike would be displayed.
translations.idiomatic: I then served as Regular Grandee and was one of the four envoys; bearing the imperial staff I proclaimed grace in the east, traveled through Qi and Lu and across Liang and Song, gathered folk songs, and examined legal cases—hoping that no voice would be lost and that praise and blame alike would come to light.

sentences.zh: 而才輕任重，多不遂心。

translations.literal: Yet my talent was light and my burden heavy; much did not accord with my wishes.
translations.idiomatic: But my abilities were slight and my responsibilities heavy, and much did not go as I had hoped.

sentences.zh: 所採之詩，並始申目，而值鑾輿南討，問罪宛鄧，臣復忝行軍，樞機是務。

translations.literal: The odes collected had only just begun to be catalogued when the imperial carriage went south on campaign to question guilt at Wan and Deng; your subject again held a post on the campaign staff, with military keys as the task.
translations.idiomatic: The poems collected had only just been entered on the register when the emperor marched south to punish Wan and Deng; I was again attached to the campaign staff, occupied with military affairs.

sentences.zh: 及輦駕之返，膳御未和，續以大諱奄臻，四海崩慕，遂爾推遷，不及聞徹。

translations.literal: When the carriage returned, the imperial meals were not yet settled; continuing with the great bereavement suddenly arriving, the four seas collapsed in mourning; thus there was deferral and transfer, and I did not reach full report.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned, the court was still in disarray; then came the sudden death of the emperor and universal mourning, and in the upheaval I never completed the submission.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改牧秦蕃，違離闕下，繼以譴疾相纏，寧丁八歲。

translations.literal: Before long I was reassigned to govern the Qin frontier, parted from below the palace gates; continuing with reproof and illness entwined, I mourned for my father for eight years.
translations.idiomatic: Soon I was transferred to govern the Qin region, far from court; then reproof and illness followed one upon another, and I spent eight years in mourning for my father.

sentences.zh: 常恐所採之詩永淪丘壑，是臣夙夜所懷，以為深憂者也。

translations.literal: I constantly feared the odes collected would forever sink into ravines and mounds—this is what your subject has harbored day and night, taking it as a deep worry.
translations.idiomatic: I constantly feared the poems I had gathered would be lost forever in obscurity—this has been my deepest worry night and day.

sentences.zh: 陛下垂日月之明，行雲雨之施，察臣往罪之濫，矜臣貧病之切，既蒙崇以祿養，復得拜掃丘墳，明目友朋，無所負愧。

translations.literal: Your Majesty sheds the brightness of sun and moon and exercises the bestowal of clouds and rain, examining the excess of your subject's past faults and pitying the urgency of my poverty and illness; having been honored with stipends for support, I was again able to sweep my ancestors' tombs—clear-eyed before friends, with nothing to bear as shame.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty shines like sun and moon and showers grace like rain, overlooking my past excesses and pitying my poverty and illness; honored with stipends for my support and allowed again to tend my family's graves, I can face my friends without shame.

sentences.zh: 且臣一二年來，所患不劇，尋省本書，粗有髣髴。

translations.literal: Moreover, for the past year or two my illness has not been severe; searching through the original book, there is a rough outline.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, over the past year or two my illness has not been grave, and reviewing the original compilation I have recovered a rough draft.

sentences.zh: 凡有七卷，今寫上呈，伏願昭覽，敕付有司，使魏代所採之詩，不堙於丘井，臣之願也。」

translations.literal: In all there are seven volumes; I now copy and present them above, humbly wishing Your Majesty would illuminate and view them and command the relevant offices, so that the odes collected in the Wei age may not be buried in wells and ravines—this is your subject's wish.
translations.idiomatic: There are seven volumes in all, which I now submit; I humbly pray Your Majesty will review them and order the proper offices to preserve the poems gathered in the Wei period from being lost to oblivion—this is my sole wish.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，侍中崔光表曰：「彝及李韶，朝列之中唯此二人出身官次本在臣右，器能幹世，又並為多，近來參差，便成替後。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Suzong's reign, Palace Attendant Cui Guang memorialized: "Yi and Li Shao—in the court ranks only these two men's origins and official seniority were originally above your subject's, yet in capacity and ability to govern the age they both excel; recently through uneven treatment they have been pushed to the rear.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaoming's reign, Palace Attendant Cui Guang memorialized: "Zhang Yi and Li Shao are the only two men in court whose family standing and seniority originally ranked above mine, yet both are gifted administrators; recently, through uneven treatment, they have been passed over.

sentences.zh: 計其階途，雖應遷陟，然恐班秩猶未賜等。

translations.literal: Calculating their stages of advancement, though they ought to be promoted and elevated, I fear their ranks and grades have still not been granted in equal measure.
translations.idiomatic: By the stages of their careers they ought to be promoted, yet I fear their ranks have still not been granted fairly.

sentences.zh: 昔衞之公叔，引下同舉；

translations.literal: In former days the Gongsun of Wei drew up those below to advance together;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Wei's Gongsun drew up his subordinates to advance together;

sentences.zh: 晉之士丐，推長伯游。

translations.literal: Jin's Shigai pushed forward the elder Boyou.
translations.idiomatic: and Jin's Shigai promoted the senior Boyou.

sentences.zh: 古人所高，當時見許。

translations.literal: What the ancients esteemed was praised and approved in their own time.
translations.idiomatic: What the ancients honored was praised and approved in their own day.

sentences.zh: 敢緣斯義，乞降臣位一階，授彼汎級，齊行聖庭，帖穆選敍。」

translations.literal: I dare follow this principle and beg to lower my rank by one step, granting them a general grade, walking together in the sage court, harmoniously aligned in selection and ordering.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to follow this principle and beg to lower my own rank by one step, granting them an equal grade so we may stand together at court in fair and harmonious order.

sentences.zh: 詔加征西將軍、冀州大中正。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him General Who Pacifies the West and Grand Rectifier of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him General Who Pacifies the West and Grand Rectifier of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 雖年向六十，加之風疾，而自強人事，孜孜無怠。

translations.literal: Though he was nearing sixty and moreover afflicted with wind illness, he still forced himself in human affairs, diligent and never slackening.
translations.idiomatic: Though nearing sixty and afflicted with wind disorder, he still drove himself in public affairs, diligent and never slackening.

sentences.zh: 公私法集，衣冠從事；

translations.literal: Public and private legal compilations, officials and gentry attending;
translations.idiomatic: He compiled public and private law codes and gathered officials and gentry to assist;

sentences.zh: 延請道俗，修營齋講；

translations.literal: inviting Daoists and lay believers, repairing and conducting fasts and lectures;
translations.idiomatic: invited Daoists and lay believers and organized fasts and lectures;

sentences.zh: 好善欽賢，愛獎人物。

translations.literal: loving the good and respecting the worthy, cherishing and rewarding men of talent.
translations.idiomatic: loved the worthy, cherished talent, and rewarded men of ability.

sentences.zh: 南北新舊莫不多之。

translations.literal: Whether from north or south, old or new, none failed to flock to him.
translations.idiomatic: Men old and new, from north and south, all flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 大起第宅，微號華侈，頗侮其疏宗舊戚，不甚存紀，時有怨憾焉。

translations.literal: He greatly raised mansions and residences, slightly styled as splendid and extravagant, quite slighting his distant clansmen and old kin, not greatly preserving records of them; at times there were resentments.
translations.idiomatic: He built grand mansions in a somewhat lavish style, showed little regard for distant clansmen and old kin, and at times stirred resentment.

sentences.zh: 榮宦之間，未能止足，屢表在秦州預有開援漢中之勳，希加賞報，積年不已，朝廷患之。

translations.literal: Between glory and office he could not stop at sufficiency; repeatedly he memorialized that at Qinzhou he had beforehand rendered service in opening relief for Hanzhong, hoping for added reward and recompense, year after year without end—the court was troubled by it.
translations.idiomatic: In his pursuit of rank he could not know when to stop; he repeatedly claimed credit for aiding the campaign to recover Hanzhong while governing Qinzhou and pressed for further rewards year after year until the court grew weary of it.

sentences.zh: 第二子仲瑀上封事，求銓別選格，排抑武人，不使預在清品。

translations.literal: His second son Zhongyu submitted a sealed memorial seeking to examine and separate selection standards, suppressing military men and not allowing them to enter the pure grades.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Zhongyu submitted a sealed memorial calling for revised selection standards that would exclude military men from the pure grades.

sentences.zh: 由是眾口喧喧，謗讟盈路，立榜大巷，剋期會集，屠害其家。

translations.literal: Because of this the multitude clamored, slander and abuse filled the roads; they posted placards in the great alleys, fixing a date to assemble, slaughtering and harming his household.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this public outcry and slander filled the streets; placards were posted in the main thoroughfares fixing a date for assembly to attack his household.

sentences.zh: 彝殊無畏避之意，父子安然。

translations.literal: Yi showed absolutely no fear or avoidance; father and sons remained at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi showed no fear or evasion; father and sons remained at ease.

sentences.zh: 神龜二年二月，羽林虎賁幾將千人，相率至尚書省詬罵，求其長子尚書郎始均，不獲，以瓦石擊打公門。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Shengui, nearly a thousand Feathered Forest and Tiger Guard troops went together to the Department of State Affairs to revile and curse, seeking his eldest son, Secretariat Gentleman Shijun; not obtaining him, they struck the public gates with tiles and stones.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second Shengui year, nearly a thousand Feathered Forest and Tiger Guard soldiers went together to the Department of State Affairs to revile and abuse the family, seeking his eldest son Shijun, a Secretariat Gentleman; failing to find him, they pelted the ministry gates with tiles and stones.

sentences.zh: 上下畏懼，莫敢討抑。

translations.literal: High and low were fearful; none dared suppress or restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: Officials high and low were terrified; none dared restrain them.

sentences.zh: 遂便持火，虜掠道中薪蒿，以杖石為兵器，直造其第，曳彝堂下，捶辱極意，唱呼嗸嗸，焚其屋宇。

translations.literal: They then took fire, plundering firewood and reeds along the road, using staffs and stones as weapons, going straight to his residence, dragging Yi beneath the hall, beating and humiliating him to the utmost, shouting and howling, burning his houses.
translations.idiomatic: They then seized fire, looted fuel along the road, took up staffs and stones as weapons, marched straight to his residence, dragged Zhang Yi into the courtyard, beat and humiliated him without restraint, shouting wildly as they burned his houses.

sentences.zh: 始均、仲瑀當時踰北垣而走。

translations.literal: Shijun and Zhongyu at the time leaped over the north wall and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Shijun and Zhongyu at once leaped the north wall and fled.

sentences.zh: 始均回救其父，拜伏羣小，以請父命。

translations.literal: Shijun turned back to rescue his father, bowing prostrate before the mob to beg for his father's life.
translations.idiomatic: Shijun turned back to save his father, prostrating himself before the mob to beg for his life.

sentences.zh: 羽林等就加毆擊，生投之於烟火之中。

translations.literal: The Feathered Guard and others then added beating and strikes, casting him alive into the flames and smoke.
translations.idiomatic: The guards then beat him further and cast him alive into the fire and smoke.

sentences.zh: 及得尸骸，不復可識，唯以髻中小釵為驗。

translations.literal: When the corpse was obtained it could no longer be recognized; only a small hairpin in the topknot served as identification.
translations.idiomatic: When his body was recovered it could no longer be identified; only a small hairpin in the topknot served to identify him.

sentences.zh: 仲瑀傷重走免。

translations.literal: Zhongyu, severely wounded, fled and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyu, badly wounded, escaped.

sentences.zh: 彝僅有餘命，沙門寺與其比隣，輿致於寺。

translations.literal: Yi had only a remnant of life; the Buddhist monastery neighbored him, and they carried him by litter to the monastery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi clung to life; a Buddhist monastery stood next door, and they carried him there on a litter.

sentences.zh: 遠近聞見，莫不惋駭。

translations.literal: Those near and far who heard and saw were all struck with grief and horror.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard and saw it, near and far, were struck with grief and horror.

sentences.zh: 彝臨終，口占左右上啟曰：「臣自奉國及孫六世，尸祿素餐，負恩唯靦，徒思竭智盡誠，終然靡効。

translations.literal: At the end of his life Yi dictated to those beside him a memorial above: "Your subject from serving the state through six generations has received salary without merit, bearing grace with only shame, merely thinking to exhaust wisdom and loyalty, yet in the end without effect.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Zhang Yi dictated a final memorial: "My family has served the state for six generations, receiving salary without merit and grace I have only shamed; I thought only to exhaust my loyalty, yet in the end achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 臣第二息仲瑀所上之事，益治實多，既曰有益，寧容默爾。

translations.literal: The matter submitted by your subject's second son Zhongyu in governing truly has much benefit; since it is said to be beneficial, how could it be silently tolerated?
translations.idiomatic: The proposal my second son Zhongyu submitted would in truth benefit governance greatly; if it is beneficial, how could I keep silent?

sentences.zh: 通呈有日，未簡神聽，豈圖眾忿，乃至於此。

translations.literal: It had been presented for days without yet being sifted by the divine hearing; who would have thought popular wrath would reach this point?
translations.idiomatic: It had been submitted for days without yet reaching the emperor's ear; who could have imagined public fury would come to this?

sentences.zh: 臣不能禍防未萌，慮絕殃兆，致令軍眾橫囂，攻焚臣宅。

translations.literal: Your subject could not ward off disaster before it sprouted, consider and cut off the omen of calamity, causing military masses to rampage and shout, attacking and burning your subject's residence.
translations.idiomatic: I could not forestall disaster before it sprouted or cut off the signs of calamity, and so soldiers rioted, attacked, and burned my house.

sentences.zh: 息始均、仲瑀等叩請流血，乞代臣死，始均即陷塗炭，仲瑀經宿方蘇。

translations.literal: My sons Shijun and Zhongyu knocked their heads and begged with flowing blood to die in my place; Shijun at once fell into ashes and charcoal, Zhongyu after a night barely revived.
translations.idiomatic: My sons Shijun and Zhongyu begged with blood flowing to die in my place; Shijun at once perished in the flames, and Zhongyu revived only after a night.

sentences.zh: 臣年已六十，宿被榮遇，垂暮之秋，忽見此苦，顧瞻災酷，古今無比。

translations.literal: Your subject is already sixty years old, long receiving honored favor; in the autumn of life's decline I suddenly see this suffering; looking back on the cruel disaster, there is no parallel in past or present.
translations.idiomatic: I am already sixty, long favored by the throne; in the autumn of my life I suddenly meet this agony—a cruelty without parallel in past or present.

sentences.zh: 臣傷至重，殘氣假延，望景顧時，推漏就盡，頃刻待終，臣之命也，知復何言。

translations.literal: Your subject's wounds are extremely grave; with remnant breath borrowed for extension, looking at the shadow and counting the time, pushing the clepsydra toward its end, awaiting the final moment in an instant—your subject's fate; knowing again what to say.
translations.idiomatic: My wounds are grave; on borrowed breath I watch the shadow and count the hours, the water clock nearing its end, death imminent—this is my fate, and what more can I say?

sentences.zh: 若所上之書，少為益國，臣便是生以理全，死與義合，不負二帝於地下，臣無餘恨矣。

translations.literal: If the book submitted can slightly benefit the state, your subject would then be living with principle intact and dying united with righteousness, not failing the two emperors underground—your subject has no remaining regret.
translations.idiomatic: If what we submitted can even slightly benefit the state, then I have lived with integrity and die in righteousness, not failing the two emperors in the grave—I have no further regret.

sentences.zh: 一歸泉壤，長離紫庭，戀仰天顏，誠痛無已。

translations.literal: Once returning to the springs and mounds, long parted from the purple court, cherishing and looking up at the heavenly countenance, truly pain without end.
translations.idiomatic: Once I return to the grave, forever parted from the imperial court, I shall still cherish Your Majesty's countenance—my grief will know no end.

sentences.zh: 不勝眷眷，力喘奉辭，伏願二聖加御珍膳，覆露黔首，壽保南嶽，德與日昇。

translations.literal: Unable to bear the deep attachment, with strength gasping I offer this farewell; humbly wishing the two sages would add to their precious meals, cover and shelter the black-haired people, preserve life like the southern mountains, virtue rising with the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Overcome with devotion, gasping out these words I take leave; I humbly pray the two sovereigns will guard their precious health, shelter the common people, long preserve life as the southern mountains, and let virtue rise with the sun.

sentences.zh: 臣夙被芻豢，先後銜恩，欲報之期，昊天罔極，亡魂有知，不忘結草。」

translations.literal: Your subject long received fodder and grain, successively bearing grace; the time to repay is boundless as Heaven—if the departed soul has awareness, I shall not forget the knotted grass.
translations.idiomatic: I have long been fed by the state's bounty and repeatedly received grace; the time to repay is boundless as Heaven—if my departed soul has awareness, I shall not forget to repay with knotted grass.

sentences.zh: 彝遂卒，時年五十九。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi then died, aged fifty-nine at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi then died at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 官為收掩羽林凶強者八人斬之，不能窮誅羣豎，即為大赦以安眾心，有識者知國紀之將墜矣。

translations.literal: The government for collecting and burying beheaded eight of the violent among the Feathered Guard but could not exhaustively punish the whole mob; thereupon a great amnesty was issued to settle popular hearts—those with insight knew the nation's discipline was about to fall.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities buried Zhang Yi and beheaded eight of the ringleaders among the guards but could not punish the whole mob; a general amnesty was then issued to calm the people—those with insight knew the dynasty's discipline was collapsing.

sentences.zh: 喪還所焚宅，與始均東西分斂於小屋。

translations.literal: The funeral returned to the burned residence; east and west with Shijun they were separately enshrouded in a small room.
translations.idiomatic: The funeral procession returned to the burned house; Zhang Yi and Shijun were laid out separately in a small room east and west.

sentences.zh: 仲瑀遂以創重避居滎陽，至五月，創得漸瘳，始奔父喪，詔賜布帛千匹。

translations.literal: Zhongyu then because of severe wounds avoided residence at Xingyang; by the fifth month the wounds gradually healed and he first rushed to his father's funeral; an edict bestowed a thousand bolts of cloth and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyu, severely wounded, took refuge at Xingyang; by the fifth month his wounds had healed enough for him to attend his father's funeral, and an edict granted him a thousand bolts of cloth and silk.

sentences.zh: 靈太后以其累朝大臣，特垂矜惻，數月猶追言泣下，謂諸侍臣曰：「吾為張彝飲食不御，乃至首髮微有虧落。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling, because he was a minister of many reigns, especially showed pity; for months she still spoke of it with tears, saying to the attendant ministers: "Because of Zhang Yi I have not taken my meals, even to the point that the hair on my head has slightly fallen out.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling, because he had served many reigns, showed special compassion; for months she still spoke of him in tears, telling the attendant ministers: "For Zhang Yi I have refused my meals, even until the hair on my head has begun to thin.

sentences.zh: 悲痛之苦，以至於此。」

translations.literal: The pain of grief has reached this point."
translations.idiomatic: My grief has gone as far as this."

sentences.zh: 初，彝曾祖幸，所招引河東民為州裁千餘家，後相依合，至於罷入冀州，積三十年，析別有數萬戶，故高祖比校天下民戶，最為大州。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yi's great-grandfather Xing had attracted and settled over a thousand households of Hedong people as provincial settlers; later they joined together, until dismissal and entry into Ji Province, accumulating thirty years; through division and separation there were tens of thousands of households—therefore Emperor Gaozu compared and checked the realm's household registers and [Ji] was the greatest province.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhang Yi's great-grandfather Xing had settled more than a thousand households from Hedong in the province; over thirty years they grew through division and merger to tens of thousands of households—so when Emperor Gaozu compared household registers throughout the realm, Ji ranked as the largest province.

sentences.zh: 彝為黃門，每侍坐以為言，高祖謂之曰：「終當以卿為刺史，酬先世誠效。」

translations.literal: When Yi was Attendant of the Yellow Gate, each time he sat in attendance he spoke of this; Emperor Gaozu said to him: "In the end I shall take you as inspector to reward your forebears' sincere service.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yi served as Attendant of the Yellow Gate, he raised the matter whenever he attended the emperor, who told him: "In the end I shall make you inspector to reward your ancestors' loyal service.

sentences.zh: 彝追高祖往旨，累乞本州，朝議未許。

translations.literal: Yi pursued Emperor Gaozu's former intent and repeatedly begged for his native province; court deliberation did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi pressed the emperor's earlier promise and repeatedly begged for his home province, but court deliberation did not approve.

sentences.zh: 彝亡後，靈太后云：「彝屢乞冀州，吾欲用之，有人違我此意。

translations.literal: After Yi died, Empress Dowager Ling said: "Yi repeatedly begged for Ji Province; I wished to use him—someone went against my intent in this.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Yi's death, Empress Dowager Ling said: "Zhang Yi repeatedly asked for Ji Province; I meant to grant it—someone opposed my wish.

sentences.zh: 若從其請，或不至是，悔之無及。」

translations.literal: If I had followed his request, perhaps it would not have come to this; regret is without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Had I granted his request, perhaps things would not have come to this—my regret is boundless.

sentences.zh: 乃贈使持節、衞將軍、冀州刺史，諡文侯。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was posthumously awarded Bearer of the Staff, Defender General, and Inspector of Ji Province, with the posthumous title Marquis Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was then posthumously honored as Bearer of the Staff, Defender General, and Inspector of Ji Province, with the posthumous title Marquis Wen.

sentences.zh: 始均，字子衡，端潔好學，有文才。

translations.literal: Shijun, courtesy name Ziheng, was upright, pure, and fond of learning, with literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Shijun, whose courtesy name was Ziheng, was upright, pure, and fond of learning, with literary gifts.

sentences.zh: 司徒行參軍，遷著作佐郎。

translations.literal: Staff Officer of the Grand Commandant, promoted to Assistant Gentleman of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He served as staff officer to the Grand Commandant and was promoted to Assistant Gentleman of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 世宗以彝先朝勤舊，不幸疹廢，特除始均長兼左民郎中。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong, because Yi was an old meritorious minister of the former court who had met misfortune and ruin, specially appointed Shijun long-term concurrent Left Gentleman of the Ministry of the People.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu, because Zhang Yi was a meritorious minister of the previous reign who had met a tragic end, specially appointed Shijun as long-term concurrent Left Gentleman of the Ministry of the People.

sentences.zh: 遷員外常侍，仍領郎。

translations.literal: Promoted to Supernumerary Palace Attendant, still holding the gentleman post.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Supernumerary Palace Attendant while retaining his gentleman post.

sentences.zh: 始均才幹，有美於父，改陳壽魏志為編年之體，廣益異聞，為三十卷。

translations.literal: Shijun's talent and ability had beauty surpassing his father; he revised Chen Shou's Records of Wei into annalistic form, broadly adding divergent hearsay, making thirty volumes.
translations.idiomatic: Shijun's ability surpassed his father's; he reworked Chen Shou's Records of Wei into annalistic form, adding much additional material, in thirty volumes.

sentences.zh: 又著冠帶錄及諸賦數十篇，今並亡失。

translations.literal: He also composed Record of Caps and Belts and several dozen fu rhapsodies; all are now lost.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Record of Caps and Belts and several dozen fu rhapsodies; all are now lost.

sentences.zh: 初，大乘賊起於冀瀛之間，遣都督元遙討平之，多所殺戮，積尸數萬。

translations.literal: Initially Mahayana rebels arose between Ji and Ying; Commander Yuan Yao was dispatched to suppress and pacify them, killing many until corpses piled up to tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Mahayana rebels rose in the Ji and Ying region; Commander Yuan Yao was dispatched to suppress them, killing many until corpses numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 始均以郎中為行臺，忿軍士重以首級為功，乃令檢集人首數千，一時焚爇，至於灰燼，用息僥倖，見者莫不傷心。

translations.literal: Shijun served as Gentleman on the mobile secretariat; angered that the soldiers prized enemy heads for merit, he ordered thousands of human heads collected and burned at once to ashes, to quell opportunism—all who witnessed it were grieved.
translations.idiomatic: As a director on the campaign staff, Shijun was angered that soldiers prized enemy heads for merit; he had thousands of heads gathered and burned to ash at once to curb opportunism, and all who saw it were heartsick.

sentences.zh: 及始均之死也，始末在於烟炭之間，有燋爛之痛，論者或亦推咎焉。

translations.literal: When Shijun died, from beginning to end he was amid smoke and embers, suffering the pain of scorching—commentators sometimes placed blame on this as well.
translations.idiomatic: When Shijun died, he had been caught from start to finish in smoke and fire, burned alive—some commentators blamed his earlier act for it.

sentences.zh: 贈樂陵太守，諡曰孝。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Administrator of Laoling, with the posthumous name Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Administrator of Laoling, with the posthumous name Xiao.

sentences.zh: 子暠，襲祖爵。

translations.literal: His son Hao inherited his grandfather's title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hao inherited his grandfather's title.

sentences.zh: 武定中，開府主簿。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era, [he served as] chief clerk of the opening office.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wuding era he served as chief clerk of the opening office.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, his title was reduced according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, his title was reduced according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 暠弟晏之，武定中，儀同開府中兵參軍。

translations.literal: Hao's younger brother Yanzhi, in the Wuding era, [served as] Army Aide of Equal Rank in the Opening Office.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's younger brother Yanzhi served in the Wuding era as Army Aide of Equal Rank in the Opening Office.

sentences.zh: 仲瑀，司空祭酒、給事中。

translations.literal: Zhongyu, Libationer of the Minister of Works and Supervising Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyu served as Libationer of the Minister of Works and Supervising Attendant.

sentences.zh: 子台，儀同開府參軍事。

translations.literal: His son Tai, Army Staff Officer of Equal Rank in the Opening Office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tai served as Army Staff Officer of Equal Rank in the Opening Office.

sentences.zh: 仲瑀弟珉，著作佐郎。

translations.literal: Zhongyu's younger brother Min, Assistant Gentleman of Composition.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyu's younger brother Min served as Assistant Gentleman of Composition.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：郭祚才幹敏實，有世務之長，高祖經綸之始，獨在勤勞之地，居官任事，動靜稱述。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Guo Zuo was talented, capable, and diligent in substance, with strengths in worldly affairs; at the beginning of Emperor Gaozu's grand planning he alone stood in the realm of strenuous labor—in office and charged with duties, his conduct in motion and rest was praised.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Guo Zuo was talented, practical, and quick, skilled in affairs of state; at the outset of Emperor Wen's great enterprise he alone bore the heaviest burdens, and in every office his conduct won praise.

sentences.zh: 張彝風力謇謇，有王臣之氣，銜命擁旄，風聲猶在。

translations.literal: Zhang Yi was forceful and upright, with the bearing of a king's minister; bearing credentials and waving banners, his renown still stands.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi was forceful and upright, with the air of a true minister of the throne; entrusted with command and banner, his reputation endures still.

sentences.zh: 並魏氏器能之臣乎？

translations.literal: Were they not both capable ministers of Wei?
translations.idiomatic: Were they not both able servants of Wei?

sentences.zh: 遭隨有命，俱嬰世禍，悲哉！

translations.literal: Meeting fate as it followed, both suffered calamities of the age—how tragic!
translations.idiomatic: Subject to the turns of fate, both were struck down by the calamities of their age—how tragic!

sentences.zh: 始均才志未申，惜也。

translations.literal: Shijun's talents and aspirations were unfulfilled—a pity.
translations.idiomatic: Shijun's talent and ambition were never fully realized—a pity.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation Notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation Notes

sentences.zh: 至於馬道 御覽卷二一一

translations.literal: as far as the horse ramp—Imperial Overview, vol. 211
translations.idiomatic: as far as the horse ramp—Imperial Overview, vol. 211

sentences.zh: 〈一０一一頁〉
「馬」作「馳」，當是。

translations.literal: "horse" is written as "gallop"; this is correct.
translations.idiomatic: "Horse" is written as "gallop"; this is correct.

sentences.zh: 潤沃九區 諸本「沃」訛「伏」，今據冊府卷五二三

translations.literal: moisten and enrich the nine regions—in various editions "沃" is corrupted to "伏"; now corrected per Cefu, vol. 523
translations.idiomatic: "Moisten and enrich the nine regions"—in various editions wo is corrupted to fu; corrected here per Cefu, vol. 523

sentences.zh: 〈六二四八頁〉
改。

translations.literal: corrected.
translations.idiomatic: corrected.

sentences.zh: 末蒙陛下不遺之施 諸本「末」作「未」，南本及冊府

translations.literal: finally received Your Majesty's gracious bestowal without abandonment—in various editions "末" is written as "未"; the Southern edition and Cefu
translations.idiomatic: "Finally received Your Majesty's gracious bestowal without abandonment"—in various editions mo ("finally") is written as wei ("not yet"); the Southern edition and Cefu

sentences.zh: 〈同上卷頁〉

translations.literal: 〈same volume, p.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈same volume, p.〉

sentences.zh: 作「末」。

translations.literal: have "末."
translations.idiomatic: It reads mo (finally).

sentences.zh: 按「末蒙」與上句「早荷」相對，「未」字形近而訛，今從南本。

translations.literal: "末 received" parallels "early received" in the preceding clause; "未" is a graphic near-error—follow the Southern edition.
translations.idiomatic: "Finally received" parallels "early received" in the preceding clause; wei is a graphic corruption of mo—follow the Southern edition.

sentences.zh: 侍則出入兩都 按「侍」字上或下當脫一字。

translations.literal: attending then entering and leaving the two capitals—regarding "侍," one character is probably missing above or below.
translations.idiomatic: "Attending then entering and leaving the two capitals"—the character shi ("attend") probably has a missing character above or below it.

sentences.zh: 冊府

translations.literal: Cefu
translations.idiomatic: Cefu

sentences.zh: 〈同上卷頁〉

translations.literal: 〈same volume, p.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈same volume, p.〉

sentences.zh: 作「陪侍兩宮」。

translations.literal: has "attending the two palaces."
translations.idiomatic: It reads "attending the two palaces."

sentences.zh: 「兩都」指代京和洛陽，兩宮指太后和帝，意有不同。

translations.literal: "Two capitals" refers to the Dai capital and Luoyang; "two palaces" refers to the Empress Dowager and the Emperor—the meanings differ.
translations.idiomatic: "Two capitals" means Dai and Luoyang; "two palaces" means the empress dowager and the emperor—the senses are different.
